rows.author: H072;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ridon spoke about the exorbitant fees under
“Other School Fees” (OSFs) being charged to students in primary, secondary, and even tertiary schools both in private and public schools. He said that these are an added burden to students and are likewise questionable. He maintained that it is clear that the policy of deregulation is very much alive under the
Aquino administration, with tuition and other fees doubling in the short period of his presidency. Thereafter, Rep. Ridon stated that he has filed House Resolution No. 1640 calling on the House Committee on Higher and Technical Education to investigate the Commission on Higher Education´s failure to regulate OSFs in public and private higher education institutions (HEIs). He added that the present situation is such that the very policies on education opened wide loopholes that turned learning into an expensive commodity and lucrative business,
highlighting the perils of commercialization and
deregulation. At this point, Rep. Ridon enjoined his colleagues to campaign against what he dubbed as “criminal charges” being imposed by HEIs. He also said that student leaders present in the Session Hall would distribute small lanterns to the Members signifying their Christmas wish for affordable and accessible
education for all. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.30, pp.4-5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-12-01
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: H069;
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Hicap adverted to the
birth anniversary last November 30 of Filipino hero, Gat Andres Bonifacio, who founded the Kataastaasang Kagalanggalangang Katipunan ng mga Anak ng Bayan” (KKK) and led a revolution for autonomy, democracy, and freedom from colonialism and feudalism. He pointed out that like their counterparts in said uprising, farmers, laborers, indigenous peoples,
and Filipino masses continue to suffer from violence and injustice. He cited the current problems of landlessness and control and ownership of lands by the rich families; repression and violence for advocating social justice; low wages; human rights violations; crimes committed by foreign soldiers;
destruction of natural resources by foreign businesses; and the military exercises and agreements with other countries which do not serve the national interest. He stressed that since the Philippine Revolution, nothing has changed except technology; and cited statistics on the increasing unemployment, low incomes and
salaries, and widespread and systematic poverty.
Rep. Hicap then encouraged the Body to address
the needs of the people and to pass House Bill No. 252 or the Genuine Agrarian Reform Bill; House Bill No. 253, raising workers ´wages by P125; and House Bill No. 3015, raising government employees´ salaries by P6,000.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.30,p.5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-12-01
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: H081;
rows.abstract:
In celebration of the International Human Rights
Day, Rep. Zarate spoke about certain trumped-up
charges filed against the leaders and members of
various people´s organizations. He maintained that the mentioned cases were examples of strategic lawsuits against public participation (SLAPPs) which include any civil complaint, counter-claim, cross-claim, thirdparty
complaint or complaint intervention, criminal
complaint or information filed against individuals, groups, labor unions, entities or associations, among others, the intent of which is to harass, vex or silence said individuals or groups. He pointed out that the groups advocating their valid democratic causes and
their leaders are harassed to stress them out into submission. Wondering how marginalized sectors can afford legal battles against big companies or state security forces, Rep. Zarate then stressed that Congress should establish a law that penalizes the filing of SLAPPs to include cases other than the environmental issues
covered by the writ of kalikasan and to protect the freedom of speech, peaceful assembly, and redress of grievances. He pointed out trumped-up charges have also been filed against private individuals such as scientists and agriculturists and cited the details thereof.
Rep. Zarate subsequently enumerated data on the
continuing violation of human rights by the military and police forces including the violent dispersal of mass actions; harassment of children and women; attacks against educational, medical, and religious organizations; and kidnapping, torture and extrajudicial killings. He asked his colleagues to arm the people with a law to punish those who initiate SLAPP charges. He reminded them that the United Nations´ theme for the commemoration of the International Declaration of Human Rights on December 10, was Human Rights 365. (SOURCE: House Journal No.33,pp.8&9)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-12-09
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G105;
rows.abstract:
Upon Rep. Bondoc´s motion, the Chair recognized
Rep. De Jesus who stressed that despite the
pronouncements of President Benigno S. Aquino III to crush the state of impunity in the country, human rights violations against marginalized sectors have increased and worsened because of the government´s lack of interest to prosecute the guilty and to protect the victims. Citing the name of “Impunity King” that local and international human rights advocates have
given the President, she cited the lack of action on several cases of extrajudicial killing, kidnapping, and disappearance. She relayed how the government was giving special favors to alleged human rights violators but inhumanely treating political prisoners. As the government keeps on denying the continuing
culture of impunity in the country and puts the
blame on the victims and the judicial system instead, Rep. De Jesus enjoined her colleagues to look into the implementation of the Inter-agency Committee on Extra-legal Killings, Enforced Disappearances, Torture and other Grave Violations of the Right to Life, Liberty
and Security of Persons and called on Congress to
pursue the goals and mandate of human rights conventions and probe government officials in their crusade against human rights violations and impunity. (SOURCE: House Journal No.33,p.9)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-12-09
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: A060;
rows.title_short: Minimum Take-home Pay Of Government Employees
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ocampo informed the Body of her advocacy
to promote government employees´ welfare and benefits, in particular, how this had been affected under the 2015 General Appropriations Act by the provision therein, legislating a decrease in the minimum net take-home pay of a government employee to P3,000 monthly in contravention of the collective will of the
Members to provide benefits to government employees and the President´s budget proposal for a P4,000 net take-home pay. She explained that the meager amount resulted from the “bartering” by Members of the Senate with
certain vested interests during the Conference Committee deliberations. She lamented how the House conferees had failed to defend the position of the House and the welfare of civil servants. She also questioned Senator Francis Escudero for contesting the increase in the workers´ net mimum take-home pay by maintaining the level of P3,000 monthly. Rep. Ocampo said she agreed with the request of the Speaker and the Majority Leader to call for a voting on the ratification of the conference committee report
on the 2015 national budget to unite the leadership. She however urged the chair of the Committee on Appropriations to call for an investigation on the malpractice of automatic payroll deduction for loans incurred by government employees from private lenders.
She hoped to get the support and commitment of
the leadership to change the situation of the government employees whose salaries had remained the same despite the four-step increases provided for under the latest Salary Standardization Law. (SOURCE: House Journal No.35,p.10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-12-15
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F102;
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Walden F. Bello
from Akbayan Party-List spoke on the issue of the
Pandacan Oil Depot, this as he joined the ordinary residents of Pandacan, the city of Manila, the various government and private organizations, and the past and incumbent
Representatives from said city, in celebrating
the November 25 decision of the Supreme Court directing the big oil companies Petron, Chevron and Shell, to finally close and relocate the oil depot. He also recognized and commended their efforts in upholding the cause for the past 14 years. In behalf of Akbayan, Rep. Bello urged Congress first, to monitor the compliance of said companies to the Supreme Court decision, citing specifically the negative actions of Shell on the issue. Secondly, he asked his colleagues to monitor the clean-up,rehabilitation
and development plans for the site which he
opined should be undertaken by the city government of Manila and its citizens.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Upon recognition of the Chair, Rep. Jose L. Atienza Jr. recalled the issues and the challenges that his administration had faced when he was still the mayor of Manila to ensure the complete relocation of the Pandacan Oil Depot. He stated for the record that the November
25 Supreme Court decision stemmed from a case that he, together with other proenvironment
groups and individuals, had filed questioning a local ordinance passed during the term of former Manila Mayor Alfredo Lim by the city council headed by Vice Mayor Isko Moreno, allowing the permanent stay of the oil depot. He thanked Akbayan for fully appreciating the issues but still urged the group and the others involved to remain vigilant and continue their fight until
the oil depot is relocated. Rep. Bello agreed with Rep. Atienza and then expressed hope that the city government of Manila will involve its citizens and the civil society groups in planning
for a new Pandacan.  
(SOURCE: House Journal No.37,p.5)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-12-17)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Atienza. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H065;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Atienza spoke in opposition to the recommendation of certain Senators to reimpose the death penalty in reaction to news reports about the special considerations and accommodations afforded to some individuals and convicted criminals in the New Bilibid Prison (NBP). He stated that death penalty is not the
solution because it will not address the real problem of mismanagement and corruption in prison management. Rep. Atienza thereafter explained that the proposed reimposition of death penalty would be a travesty under a crooked judicial and criminal justice system
implemented by corrupt authorities and is not the
solution to address the blatant corruption and mismanagement by law enforcement authorities. He said that the action of Justice Secretary Leila de Lima immediately absolving the NBP´s management from culpability for the excessive privileged treatment of incarcerated drug lords and continued violation of the laws is in itself questionable considering that the NBP is under
the immediate jurisdiction and responsibility of the Department of Justice (DOJ). This is the reason that he has to ask for a congressional investigation, he added. Thereupon, Rep. Atienza reiterated the position of Party-List Buhay on the issue of death penalty and put forth the reasons against its reimposition citing that
death penalty can never be a lawful and moral solution as it is a distortion of the sacredness of life and the political and economic inequality that persists in the Filipino
society.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.37,pp.5&6)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-12-17)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee

rows.author: H080;
rows.title_short: Executed O F W In Saudi
rows.abstract:
Rep. Señeres took to task the concerned Philippine government officials for their failure to stop the beheading of Carlito Lana, an overseas Filipino worker (OFW) in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and asked that the Committees on Overseas Workers Affairs, and Foreign Affairs invite Vice President Jejomar Binay; the Presidential Adviser on OFWs, Foreign Affairs
Secretary Albert del Rosario; and Labor Secretary
Linda Baldoz, to determine the official acts of the Philippine government in stopping the beheading of Carlito Lana. Rep. Señeres maintained that the congressional investigation
would help elicit the facts on whether the
Philippine government, through the DFA and the Philippine Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, the Office of the Vice President, the DOLE and the POEA and their respective representatives, had proceeded with the necessary diplomatic and labor protocols to represent the legal interests of Carlito Lana before the Saudi government.
He claimed that the failure of the Philippine government to come to the aid of Carlito Lana would be doubly unfortunate if there was undue legal influence and interference by the Saudi government on the case and if there was a failure on the part of the Philippine government to ask for the commutation of the OFW´s death sentence from the King of Saudi Arabia for any
mitigating and just cause. 
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Rep. Dela Cruz raised the issue on whether the
Philippine Ambassador to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia had done the necessary diplomatic and labor protocols to commute the death sentence of Carlito Lana. In answer, Rep. Señeres maintained that the proposed congressional investigation on this case would help determine whether the representatives of the Philippine government had done everything to protect Carlito Lana as it was apparent from reliable news reports and information that had been provided to him by the
Philippine Embassy in Saudi Arabia that the Philippine Ambassador, who should be personally held responsible for the life of the migrant worker, was himself caught unaware by the beheading of Carlito Lana. To another query of Rep. Dela Cruz, Rep. Señeres said that the Chairperson of the Committee on Overseas
Workers Affairs had already consented to his request to summon Vice President Binay, the Foreign Affairs Secretary and the Labor Secretary to enlighten the Members on what happened to Mr. Lana.
REMARKS OF REP. BELLO (W.)
Rep. Bello informed the Body that as chairperson
of the Committee on Overseas Workers Affairs, he has committed to conduct a committee hearing calling the concerned officials to account for what happened to the OFW who was beheaded in Saudi Arabia. Moreover, he said that Saudi Arabia should be condemned for continuing a barbaric practice of beheading as its penalty for death and should not join the ranks of civil
society until such practice is eliminated.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.37,p.5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2015-02-09
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Dela Cruz, manifestation by Rep.Bello,W. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F100;
rows.abstract:
Citing his personal experience in several instances, Rep. Neri J. Colmenares complained about Cebu Pacific Airlines´ late and delayed arrival of its planes, charging of penalties for re-booking, nonoperation of landing tubes and other facilities, misleading promotions, constant amount of surcharges and taxes despite the decrease in the price of crude oil - all meant to save on costs at the expense and in disregard of the rights of consumers. He said he would file a resolution to inquire on the matter in order to protect public interest.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.36,p.3)

rows.author: F093;
rows.abstract:
In commemoration of the International Migrants
Day, Rep. Ilagan spoke on the adoption by the United Nations of the International Convention on the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers and their Families (ICRMW), and the role of Filipino migrant workers in the global economy and the nation´s social development.
She however lamented that even as the government
has maintained efforts to export Filipino labor
abroad in order to ease domestic unemployment, it has not given Filipino migrant workers the attention and program they deserve even though they continue to be the milking cow of the government. She further noted how the government has also slashed the funds for direct overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) services, which get only one percent of the aggregate funds of the national budget. She maintained that despite the
enactment of the Overseas Absentee Voting Law, the OFWs continue to be politically disenfranchised.  Rep. Ilagan enjoined his colleagues to build a legislative platform for the political empowerment of the migrant workers, institute genuine agrarian reform,
and launch national industrialization in order to give the OFWs secured and lasting jobs in the country. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.36,pp.3&4)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-12-16
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G034;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Dimaporo clarified the issues that had cast
adverse aspersions to her family pertaining to the assassination attempt on Rep. Vicente F. Belmonte Jr., of the Lone District of Iligan City and to express her concerns on the health and safety of Rep. Belmonte and the wounded victims. She also expressed her condolences
to the families of the murdered staff, and to reiterate the appeal to law enforcement officials to maintain peace and order in said congressional district. She explained that the portrayal of the Dimaporos as masterminding the assassination of Rep. Belmonte is not only a demolition job against her family, but also
a politically motivated scheme perpetrated by paid hacks in media to deliberately take the heat off and deflect responsibility from certain personalities and the mastermind of the dastardly act and heinous crime and to mislead the authorities. She also maintained that in
the interest of truth, justice, transparency, and journalistic integrity, the Philippine Daily Inquirer and the ANC News Network should corroborate the contents of their unverified news reports. In contravening further the allegations pinning the assassination attempt on Rep. Belmonte (V.) on the Dimaporos, Rep. Dimaporo (I.) explained that such prejudicial
allegation is without basis inasmuch as the Dimaporos do not have any political stake in the politics of the Lone District of Iligan City and that they are very much politically marginalized defending themselves from the alleged power grab by Abdullah “Dabs” Mangotara and his cohorts who had been employing both political and nefarious criminal means, to gain power in Lanao del Norte. She thereafter elaborated on the local political situation in Lanao del Norte alleging that the harsh and violent politics in the province and against the Dimaporos had been caused by the “band of rogues and thugs” of the Mangotaras and their equally criminally-minded conspirators. She stated that if anything violent will befall the members of her family, the dastardly act would be without doubt
the result of collective act of Abdullah Mangotara and his minions. Thereafter inquiring on the status of the cases filed against Commissioner Mangotara and Mayor Lacson Lantud for the possession of firearms and ammunitions
and the investigation of the case against Mr. Casan Maquiling, she submitted to the House Secretariat a copy of the letter addressed to the President detailing the circumstances of the murder case filed against said commissioner, with copies thereof furnished to concerned
government officials and offices, House Members,
television and radio stations, and other media
outlets. She moved that the same be taken as part of her privilege speech. At this point, the Chair directed the Secretary General
to accept as part of Rep. Dimaporo´s (I.) speech
the said letter.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.36,pp.4-5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-12-16
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: A013;
rows.title_short: Year - End And Christmas Message Of Speaker Belmonte
rows.abstract:
My esteemed colleagues, let me extend my profound
thanks for your steadfast dedication to this
Chamber´s work throughout the year. Because of your hard work, we were able to pass the General Appropriations Act (GAA) yet again on schedule, in fact for the fifth straight year. Since 2011, a reenacted budget has become a thing of the past. I trust that the timely passage of the 2015 GAA will enable the government to roll out its programs and projects thereby ensuring the continued delivery of vital services to all our people. Congratulations are also due to all of us for our efforts in assisting our people during the most recent typhoon to hit our country, so close to the Christmas season at that. Although this year´s Ruby was less severe
than last year´s Yolanda, Ruby nevertheless inflicted losses in lives and property in no small measure. The good news is that relief operations conducted by both the national and the local governments were up and running before, during, and after Ruby´s landfall.
The implementation of emergency measures, including the prompt evacuation of thousands, if not hundreds of thousands of people in affected areas, was key to saving so many lives. Underlying all these, I believe, is the strong spirit of solidarity among Filipinos, especially during times of calamities and disasters. That spirit has shown bright once more. Different
families were helping each other seek shelter as
Ruby lashed at their communities. This good news of Filipinos helping one another is heartwarming and humbling. May I say also that the approval of the supplemental budget for 2014 is also important, because urgent infrastructure, socioeconomic rehabilitation and reconstruction projects, which are not funded in existing
laws, need to be funded and commenced at the earliest possible time. However, an even greater challenge to the rehabilitation of typhoon-affected areas will be to provide the means by which victims can be genuinely empowered. We should not merely rebuild damaged infrastructure and property, or restore means of livelihood, or resume disrupted classes. We should also restore hope, confidence and resolve in individuals,
families, and communities. It is only through genuine empowerment that our people can truly live their own lives, fend for their own families, and carve their own futures. We need to be able to provide more jobs and opportunities
for our people. Indeed, we can never be satisfied with the status quo. In fact, to be satisfied with this status quo is to go backward. We must continuously move forward with the transformation of our economy and society.
On that regard, I am encouraged by the performance of our 16th Congress. Our harvest of meaningful and responsible legislation reflects your consistent hard work. As of December 17, 2014, and not counting some of those that we approved today, we have processed 1,686 measures of which 20 were enacted into laws and 350 were approved on Third and final reading by this Chamber and sent to the Senate. Notably, apart from the 2015 GAA that provides for the most transparent and most detailed budget we have ever had, we have enacted key laws that bear on
our country´s economic growth and productivity.
For instance, Republic Act No.10635, 
“Establishing the MARINA as the Single Maritime Administration.” Now this really helps all our seamen abroad. Republic Act No.10638, “Extending the Corporate Life of Philippine National Railways for Another 50 Years.” Republic Act No. 10641, “Allowing the Full Entry of Foreign Banks.” Republic Act No. 10644, “Promoting Job Generation and Inclusive Growth Through the Development of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.” Republic Act No. 10645, “Providing for the Mandatory PhilHealth Coverage for all Senior Citizens. ”Republic Act No.10647 No. “Strengthening the Ladderized
Interface Between Technical-Vocational Education
and Training and Higher Education.” Republic Act No. 10648, “Providing Scholarship Grants to Top Graduates of all Public High Schools.” Of course, there remains no room for complacency
even as we continue to push vital measures. Recently, we assured members of foreign and local chambers of commerce, our continuous support and action on measures which pursue greater economic competitiveness, trade and job generation and sustained economic growth. I am pleased to note that remarkable progress has
been made on a number of these priority measures.
Most of the House bills backed by business and the private sectors have been approved or close to being approved by concerned committees.
I am also happy to inform everyone that we are
about to transmit to the President the bill that would increase the tax exemption cap for 13th month pay and other benefits. This will benefit the working class from both public and private sectors in terms of higher disposable income, and boost the economy in terms of greater consumption expenditures. The further growth of our economy and improvement of the welfare of our people cannot happen in an environment where peace and stability are not genuinely widespread. This is why our continuing work on
the Bangsamoro Basic Law is very important.
I would like to congratulate that special committee because they have completed the 30 or so consultations that they have programmed until this time. Congratulations to all of you. I am pleased that we unanimously passed on Third and final Reading a measure providing for the inclusion of Moro history, culture and identity studies as an elective subject in the higher
education curriculum. Indeed, even as we are about to go on our Christmas break, let us take healthy pride in what we have accomplished together. Once more, let me express my deepest and sincerest gratitude for your support and hard work. Let us all continue to work for authentic economic and social measures that will transform our nation and our people. We have been showing that we have the capacity to do it. Let us do it. Let us see this good work that we have started through to its desired conclusion.
Storms of all nature are bound to happen. Nevertheless, let us remain united. Let us allow the light of the holiday season to dispel clouds of negativity, pessimism and divisiveness. Indeed, divisiveness is probably an essential part of good legislative work. Sa aking mga minamahal na mga kapwa Kinatawan dito sa Kongreso, sana ay magkaroon kayo ng makabuluhan at matiwasay na Kapaskuhan at sa nalalapit na Bagong Taon, nawa´y higit na tayong pagpalain ng ating Panginoong Maykapal. I am very sure of it. Let us do more, even more in the coming year.
Maraming salamat. Merry Christmas, Happy
New Year sa lahat.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.37,pp.11&12)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-12-17)

rows.author: F048;
rows.abstract:
On further motion of Rep. Ortega, (F.), the Chair
recognized Rep. Emil L. Ong from the Second District of Northern Samar who initially mentioned one of Pope Francis´ touching moments during his recent visit to the Philippines, particularly his meeting with a 12-year old girl at the University of Santo Tomas whose question why God allows children to suffer caught the Holy Father speechless. He then called on his colleagues to pay attention to the most neglected sector of Philippine society - the
millions of children between two to six years old who are supposed to be the hope of the fatherland but who, due to poverty, are left to shape their own lives and are vulnerable to sad and brutal experiences. He said that this is tantamount to criminal neglect by the government
because it has no program to address their specific and unique needs which should be its priority and critical concern. In light thereof, Rep. Ong proposed that Congress should enact a bill on Early Child Education (ECE) Program which will restructure the entire education
system that would integrate early child education into the basic school system to be handled by the barangays. He suggested volunteerism as the program´s core concept and that the Department of Education should
design the ECE curriculum, prepare the instruction materials, and oversee the implementation of the program. He added that Congress can set aside a fraction of the Internal Revenue Allotment (IRA) to fund the
program at the barangay level. Finally, he answered the question posed by the young girl to Pope Francis by emphasizing that it is the government, and not God, who should be blamed for the suffering of the young, poor children.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Jose L. Atienza Jr.
asked whether the government has the proper means to take care of the poor and the street children. Rep. Ong replied that he has already drafted a bill on the implementation of the Early Child Education (ECE) Program and that he would welcome any suggestion that Rep. Atienza would wish to add regarding the matter and likewise asked whether he would like to be a coauthor thereof. Rep. Atienza said that he would be proud to cosponsor any measure that Rep. Ong will introduce to address the problem of street children and on any measure that would look into how the funds allotted to the Department of Social Welfare and Development
(DSWD) are being used. He pointed out that the solution to the problem of street children should start with the DSWD, it being the agency tasked and entrusted with the funds to address them. Rep. Ong stated that the emphasis of the ECE bill would be on the barangay officials who would handle the responsibility of taking care of the street children and that they would be accountable to the people considering that they are elected officials. As to the funds that would be allotted to the barangays for this purpose, Rep. Ong replied that he would file a bill asking Congress to allot separate funding for the implementation of the ECE Program.
Finally, Rep. Atienza asked that remedies be made
so they would know how the funds allotted for the
poor, specifically the Conditional Cash Transfer
(CCT) Program of the DSWD, are being used. He also pushed for the enactment of laws which would be more effective in support of the street children. Rep. Atienza thereafter assured Rep. Ong of his full support for any measure he would introduce on the matter. The Chair then recognized Rep. Raul V. Del Mar for a manifestation.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. DEL MAR
Rep. Del Mar interposed some observations on the
topic of Rep. Ong´s speech and congratulated the latter on his desire to file a bill to pursue his concerns regarding young children. He then expressed belief that 1) the Members would heed and do their best to live by Pope Francis´ exhortation in urging people at all levels to reject corruption in every form, with political
leaders maintaining honesty, integrity and commitment to the common good, and 2) God will not let them down if they live by these commitments.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.38,p.12)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-01-20
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Atienza; Manifestation by Rep.Del Mar. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H069;
rows.abstract:
In commemoration of the 28th year-anniversary of
the Mendiola massacre on January 22, 2015, Rep.
Hicap, speaking in Filipino, sought justice for the 13 farmers who were killed in Mendiola during the regime of the late President Corazon C. Aquino and promised to continue the fight of the peasants and farmers in their pursuit of genuine agrarian reform and national industrialization. He cited several injustices committed by the present Administration under the leadership of President Benigno S. Aquino III which included, among others, the monopoly and control of land by landlords, the expropriation and auction of thousands of hectares of agricultural land to foreign corporations, the implementation of denationalization, liberalization, privatization,
deregulation, and labor contractualization policies; and the discretionary use of agri funds. He underscored that he and the Members of different party-list groups whose advocacy is the welfare of the farmers and the marginalized have been pushing for the immediate enactment of House Bill No. 252 or the Genuine Agrarian Reform Bill, and other bills aimed at improving the plight of the farmers and the poor.
REMARKS OF DEPUTY SPEAKER APOSTOL
Upon recognition by the Chair, Deputy Speaker
Sergio A.F. Apostol asked whether he would be allowed to interpellate Rep. Hicap, to which the latter replied that he was willing to answer questions in Tagalog. Stating that Tagalog is a dialect and not an official language of the Philippines, Deputy Speaker Apostol noted that since Rep. Hicap was speaking in Tagalog,
he should have an interpreter considering that the Constitution, according to him, provides that the country´s official languages are “Pilipino” with a “P” and English.
He then asked Rep. Hicap whether he would allow
his interpellation in English. As representative of the farmers and fisherfolks, Rep. Hicap appealed to Deputy Speaker Apostol to use
the Filipino language, to which the latter stressed that he is also a farmer but a Waray farmer.
REMARKS OF THE CHAIR
The Chair suggested that Deputy Speaker Apostol
may pose his questions in English while Rep. Hicap may respond in Filipino.
INTERPELLATION OF DEPUTY SPEAKER APOSTOL
Deputy Speaker Apostol inquired whether Rep.
Hicap was aware that most agrarian reform beneficiaries have become real estate brokers.
Rep. Hicap replied in the negative but admitted to being aware of the perennial problem of landlessness among Filipino peasants despite the implementation of the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program (CARP), citing specifically the case of Hacienda Luisita farmers. Before Rep. Hicap could continue with his answers, Deputy Speaker Apostol requested that the former
translate his answers in English as previously
agreed upon.
PARLIAMENTARY INQUIRY OF REP. COLMENARES
Upon recognition of the Chair, Rep. Neri J. Colmenares inquired whether there is a rule specifying the language to be used in plenary sessions to which the Chair replied that there was an agreement that Deputy Speaker Apostol could pose his questions in English and Rep. Hicap could answer in Filipino. In view thereof, Rep. Colmenares noted that Rep. Hicap was therefore not required to answer the questions
in English anymore if he already replied in Filipino.
REMARKS OF DEPUTY SPEAKER APOSTOL
In reaction, Deputy Speaker Apostol remarked
that based on the Constitution, the official language of the country is “Pilipino” with a “P” and not Tagalog and English.
REMARKS OF REP. COLMENARES
Rep. Colmenares opined that Rep. Hicap was using
the Filipino language.
SUSPENSION OF SESSION
INTERPELLATION OF DEPUTY SPEAKER APOSTOL
(Continuation)
Reps. Apostol and Hicap further discussed about
the lands that should have been distributed to the Hacienda Luisita farmers and the status of agrarian reform in the country. The former opined that CARP had only deceived the farmer-beneficiaries. Deputy Speaker Apostol thereafter ended his interpellation saying that he and Rep. Hicap were having a communication gap.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.39,pp.6-7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-01-20
rows.remarks: Remarks & Interpellation by Rep. Apostol; Parlimentary Inquiry & Remarks by Rep. Colmenares. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G012;
rows.abstract:
After saying that the liberation of Luzon was made possible by the heroism and sacrifice of Filipino soldiers with the help of American forces, Rep. Bataoil said that the country is facing a new foreign intruder. He cited the People´s Republic of China which is claiming the West Philippine Sea and pointed out that it has one of the highest military budgets, air forces,
and military forces in the world. He thus urged the government to strengthen the nationalism and defense capability of the citizenry so that it could defend the Republic once again. He mentioned such measures as teaching nationalism and national defense in schools, organizing local defense and disaster response units,
and enacting a law to strengthen the military reserve force training of the youth.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.39,pp.7-8
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-01-21
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F122;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Dela Cruz adverted to the recent pastoral visit of Pope Francis to the country and discussed the latter´s exhortation to bring the light of Jesus to the geographical and existential peripheries of society. He quoted the Pontiff´s pronouncements in this regard
when he was still a cardinal in Argentina and during the talks he gave and masses he celebrated in the Philippines. He urged Congress to act on these messages by addressing the plight of ordinary families, overseas workers, commuters and consumers, and the jobless
and displaced as well as those who control the resources of the country.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.40,p.8)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-01-21
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H068;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Gutierrez from Party-List Akbayan spoke in
defense of the rights and welfare of public and private sector employees in the country who continue to suffer from unjust labor policies and practices, focusing on the plight of workers in government-owned and controlled corporations (GOCCs) and government financial institutions (GFIs). He explained how the promulgation of Executive Order (EO) No. 7 and the enactment
of Republic Act (RA) No. 10149 or the “GOCC
Governance Act of 2011,” have failed to secure the rights and welfare of GOCC employees since these have taken away the power of the workers, through collective bargaining agreements (CBAs), in negotiating for better and improved working conditions. Moreover, Rep. Gutierrez underscored that with the implementation of EO No. 7 and RA 10149, the unfair salary grade and position classification system in state enterprises was further compounded by the discontinuance of the traditional benefits previously enjoyed by the GOCC employees and the abolition of the Corporate Incentive Program. He added that the
routine disregard of collective negotiations agreements (CNAs) and CBAs are also apparent in various other GOCCs. After mentioning several public corporations which likewise reduced employee salaries and benefits, Rep. Gutierrez pointed out that RA No. 10149 failed to provide for the right to collective bargaining in public offices. He urged his colleagues to protect
this right in order to protect the working class from unjust labor practices.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.40,pp.1-2)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-01-26
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: H081;
rows.title_short: Cutting Of Trees In S M Baguio
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Bondoc, the Chair next recognized Rep. Carlos Isagani T. Zarate from Bayan Muna Party-List who condemned the cutting down of 30-year old pine trees in Luneta Hill in Baguio City by SM Prime Holdings to give way to its Sky Park project. Citing Pope Francis who recently visited the Philippines and advocated environment protection and mercy and compassion, he criticized the hypocrisy of promoting big business interests at the expense of the
environment and pointed out that only 17 percent of the 60 trees survived in their transfer site. Speaking in Filipino, he discussed private-sector and legislative efforts to stop and investigate the tree-cutting and the litigation thereon. In ending his speech, Rep. Zarate stressed that Baguio City´s air, greenery, and biodiversity should be protected; development must be sustainable; and the House should conduct an investigation on what he called “a massacre of the environment.” (SOURCE: House Journal No.40,p.2)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-01-26
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: G105;
rows.title_short: Hiding Of The Poor During The Pope's Visit
rows.abstract:
Initially adverting to Pope Francis´ pastoral visit to the country, Rep. De Jesus took note of his message to learn how to cry for the poor, the hungry, homeless, and abused children; various grievances presented to the Pontiff including land reform, justice for political
prisoners, and women empowerment; President Benigno S. Aquino III´s welcome remarks where he expressed resentment against church officials; and the excessive security measures for said visit. Thereupon, Rep. De Jesus mentioned the denials and alibis made by the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) in gathering the homeless and street families during the papal visit and putting them in a camp-out activity in a resort and asked where the funding for such activity came from. As the DSWD had explained that said activity for the poor was planned ahead of time and part of the assessment procedure in the modified Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) program of the government, Rep. De Jesus called on Congress to investigate the matter, ferret out the truth, and initiate concrete actions on the CCT program. She then enjoined her colleagues to uphold Pope Francis´ call to alleviate the plight of the poor with utmost sincerity.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Both speaking in Filipino, Reps. Atienza and De
Jesus discussed the manipulation made on the homeless people and street families by the government and statements of denials and alibis by the DSWD on the matter. Rep. De Jesus affirmed that such incident is an affront on the poor, a violation of their human rights and one form of corrupting reality. She stated that she
had called for an investigation on the matter in order to ferret out the truth, make the culprits accountable for their actions, and for a review of the CCT budget. Rep. Atienza thereupon expressed his support to Rep. De Jesus and called on Congress to conduct a formal congressional inquiry on the matter considering
that the mandate of the DSWD is to alleviate the
poor and not to abuse their human rights. He stressed how the government tried to hide poverty from a man who came to the country precisely to address this problem, and expressed support to Rep. De Jesus´ call to find the truth and prosecute the guilty.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.40,p.2)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-01-26
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Atienza. Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: F102;
rows.title_short: Baguio Tree Cutting By S M
rows.abstract:
As a supplement to the earlier privilege speech of Rep. Zarate on the same topic, Rep. Bello joined the Baguio City residents in expressing their outrage over the pine tree-cutting acts of SM Prime Holdings. He then asked the following questions that he hoped would be answered in a congressional hearing: why the Baguio City government, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), and the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) permitted the cutting of the pine trees; why the DENR had hastily issued the environmental compliance certificate (ECC) for the tree cutting, despite the total log ban; when did the DPWH approve the SM expansion plan and why it permitted the circumvention of Baguio City´s zoning regulations; and how many more trees will be allowed by the Baguio government and concerned
agencies to be cut in preparation for the implementation of Baguio City´s comprehensive land use plan. In conclusion, Rep. Bello said that Baguio City used to be a symbol of a modernized community with the preservation of indigenous culture and harmonious coexistence of human settlements with the beauty of
nature. He then asked Congress to stop the conversion of the City before it is too late. (SOURCE: House Journal No.40,p.18)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-01-26
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee.on Rules.

rows.author: H071;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Masongsong spoke about the appalling
services and possible violation of the legislative franchise of the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP), and which he attributed to the failure of the Electric Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA) since 2010 to fulfill its mandate of providing adequate electric supply, particularly to the people of
North Eastern Mindano Area (NEMA). He opined that
NGCP´s inefficient and inadequate performance in the area is a wake-up call for Congress to protect the Filipino people from the insidious intentions of foreign capitalists. This, as he named certain high-ranking officials of the NGCP whom he assumed to be of Chinese nationality.
He then called on his colleagues to conduct a
thorough investigation on the possible violation of the NGCP franchise to prevent further sufferings of the people. (SOURCE: House Journal No.41,p.1)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-01-27
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: F122;
rows.title_full: DEATH OF P N P - S A F TROOPS IN MAMASAPANO, MAGUINDANAO
rows.title_short: Killing Of S A F In Maguindanao
rows.abstract:
Rep. Dela Cruz spoke about the recent death of
several members of the elite Special Action Force
(SAF) of the Philippine National Police (PNP), whom he claimed were just doing their duty to uphold the law, at the hands of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) in Maguindanao. He emphasized that the MILF is not a legal entity
and what they did was a criminal act that should not go unpunished. He criticized the present administration for viewing the incident as an obstacle to the advancement of the Bangsamoro Basic Law (BBL), which had to be managed at all cost; as well as its insensitivity to the plight of its citizens. He then proposed that: the House stop all deliberations on the BBL until the truth is known and culprits are identified; appropriate committees should investigate the matter and make a public report thereon; the Members must closely monitor the justice
process on the case; a House resolution be adopted, directing all government offices to observe half-mast flags on the seventh day after the massacre; and the House would send letters of condolences to the victims´ families and set aside support funds for them. Lastly, he requested his colleagues to offer a moment
of silent prayer for the fallen cops.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BATAOIL
Upon recognition of the Chair, Rep. Leopoldo N.
Bataoil, who informed the Body that he was a SAF
battalion commander in 1992, expressed sadness and grief for the perished troopers and joined the request of Rep. Dela Cruz to have the Philippine flags flown at half-mast as a fitting tribute to the policemen who risked their lives to accomplish a legitimate mission. For his part, Rep. Dela Cruz expressed support to Rep. Bataoil´s suggestion for the declaration of a national day of mourning in honor of the slain
policemen. 
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
After agreeing to the proposal to give proper
commendations to the slain policemen, Rep. Atienza discussed with Rep. Dela Cruz his following concerns: why and how the SAF members were killed in the encounter, who were involved in the operation and who should be responsible for these deaths, and whether the House should continue with the deliberations on the BBL considering that the root cause of the massacre was not yet solved. Rep. Atienza expressed his support to Rep. Dela Cruz´s call for the conduct of a congressional inquiry on the matter to ascertain the proper government agency tasked with law enforcement and improve the statutes on law enforcement; as well as to review the conduct of deliberations on the BBL. Finally, he
signified his intent to coauthor any resolution to be filed by his colleague on the matter.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. SEMA
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Bai Sandra A.
Sema expressed her sincere condolences to the
families of the slain police officers and members of the MILF who were killed in the Maguindanao incident. She pointed out that the incident is a test of their determination in their effort to establish normalcy and to end the decades of war in the region. She assured them that she and her fellow Muslim legislators will investigate the case with objectivity in order to bring out its root cause. She assured her colleagues that the incident will not become a stumbling block to the Bangsamoro people´s pursuit of peace and happiness. 
INTERPELLATION OF REP. LOONG
Rep. Loong initially stated that the Ad Hoc
Committee on the BBL had already informed the
appropriate authorities to immediately investigate the incident which he deemed as uncalled for because of the ongoing congressional hearings on the BBL. Reps. Loong and Dela Cruz then talked about the ceasefire agreement between the government and the MILF; the MILF´s allegation that what happened was a “misencounter”; and whether or not there was proper coordination between the government and the MILF concerning the SAF operation in Maguindanao.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ACEDILLO
The Chair next recognized Rep. Francisco Ashley
L. Acedillo who, in his interpellation, supported Rep. Dela Cruz´ contention that what happened in Maguindanao was not a “misencounter” as claimed by the MILF. Rep. Acedillo then went on to explain what transpires when there is a misencounter. He expressed belief that what happened in Maguindanao involved an intent on the part of the MILF to kill the SAF members
whom it did not consider as friendly forces despite belonging to the government with whom it has forged a ceasefire agreement due to the BBL.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. LOBREGAT
Rep. Lobregat stressed his desire for truth and
peace and a BBL that is just, fair, and consistent with the Constitution and national laws; and asked Rep. Dela Cruz for his opinion thereon... At the outset, Rep. Lobregat informed the Body that in its executive sessions the previous day and that morning, the Ad Hoc Committee on the BBL had decided to (1) continue line-by-line the deliberations on the provisions of the BBL except those on national defense and security and public order, a separate AFP
command, the chief minister´s authority over the AFP, and the shape of the normalization proceedings; (2) lengthen its sessions; and (3) have Members attending the executive sessions be considered present in the plenary proceedings. He said that he had asked the Committee to condemn the killings and show reverence for the victims and to suspend the deadline for individual amendments on the BBL; and had
cancelled a vital local meeting in order to attend all executive sessions.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. LOBREGAT (Continuation)
In reaction to the remarks of Rep. Lobregat, Rep.
Dela Cruz agreed that Congress needs to support the peace process and to pass a BBL that would be
consistent with the laws of the land and realize the dreams and aspirations of the Mindanaoans.
(House Journal No.41,pp.1-3)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2015-01-28
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Bataoil, Atienza, Sema, Loong, Acedillo and Lobregat. Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: F093;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ilagan spoke on the nonaction of the
government to address the Beijing Platform for Action on critical areas of concern for women empowerment, such as poverty incidence, health, education, violence against women, human rights, decision-making, and environment, among others. She lamented that these areas of concern have been subjected to intensified privatization, deregulation, liberalization and neglect
and that the programs of the government only pursue the interest of the local and foreign elite and against that of women and of the Filipino people. As the Beijing Platform for Action has very admirable goals for women empowerment and development which the government has pledged to support but however failed to implement, she expressed fear that said agenda may be reduced to a meaningless piece of paper as the government continues to implement its neoliberal policies...In conclusion, Rep. Ilagan informed the Body that there is an ongoing consultation for the final review of the Beijing Platform for Action being held in Malacañang, the purpose of which is to determine how
best the government could implement the same.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.41,p.3)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-01-27
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: DEATH OF P N P - S A F TROOPS IN MAMASAPANO, MAGUINDANAO
rows.title_short: Killing Of S A F In Maguindanao
rows.abstract:
Rep. Alejano condemned the killing of the more
than 40 members of the PNP-SAF last Sunday and for which reason he had filed a resolution expressing condemnation of said killing. He condoled with the bereaved families; urged the government to make a strong stand against the incident; demanded the return of firearms and other equipment that were stolen by the MILF elements from the slain cops; and called for
a national mourning for the loss of these law enforcers. He said that the government must review the guidelines or rules of engagement set by the Ad Hoc Joint Action Group (AHJAG) because the government should not be tied up to its ceasefire agreement with the MILF. He stressed that failure to coordinate with the MILF does not warrant any killing; disagreed that a misencounter occurred in Maguindanao; expressed
sadness that there was a ground violation of the
ceasefire agreement because the peace partners were brutally killed; and uttered disgust over the nonsupport by the very commanders and leaders of the police force. He encouraged his peers to favorably consider his resolution which requests the House through the Ad Hoc Committee on the BBL to temporarily suspend the
deliberations on the measure pending the conduct of a congressional inquiry on the SAF incident. He then stressed that while the incident should not be taken lightly because the BBL is envisioned for the welfare of Muslim brothers in Mindanao, the Body also should not forget the interests of the police and military forces.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.41,pp.4-5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2015-01-28
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: H088;
rows.title_full: DEATH OF P N P - S A F TROOPS IN MAMASAPANO, MAGUINDANAO
rows.title_short: Killing Of S A F In Mindanao
rows.abstract:
Rep. Pagdilao lamented over what he termed as
the “barbaric massacre” of the best breed of policemen trained for counter-terrorism and guerilla warfare even if occupational hazard is part of it. He informed the Body that the SAF is close to his heart, being one of its founders in the 1980s together with then Philippine
Constabulary Chief Fidel V. Ramos. He stated that the policemen were just carrying out
a mandate to serve a warrant of arrest against foreign bomb expert, terrorist Zulkifli bin Hir a.k.a “Marwan” and Basil Usman who were under the MILF refuge. He noted that the dreadful killings had caused the BBL to hang in balance because their Senate counterparts had withdrawn their support from the measure due to a breach of confidence. Rep. Pagdilao warned those who intend to railroad the passage of the BBL just to meet its March 2015 deadline but believed that the Maguindanao incident should not deter the pursuit of a lasting peace for the people of Mindanao. He then expressed support on the
call to suspend the congressional hearings on the BBL and said that there is a need to reflect and learn lessons in crafting the laws to ensure the reign of peace in Mindanao. As he supports a congressional inquiry that will be based on enlightened minds not on emotion and passion, Rep. Pagdilao said that at this point, there is a
need to restore confidence among the various BBL
stakeholders. Rep. Pagdilao then appealed to Congress to review the government´s peace agreement with the MILF as well as compliance of the parties concerned with the Implementing Guidelines of the Joint Communique of May 6, 2002 and the Implementing Operational Guidelines of the GRP-MILF Agreement on the General Cessation of Hostilities. To show their sincerity to the peace process, he asked the government to require the MILF to surrender
the firearms and other equipment they stole from the fallen SAF elements and to deliver to the authorities Messrs. “Marwan” and Usman. In closing, he then asked the Members to offer a minute of silence for the policemen who perished in the tragic event.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BATAOIL
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Bataoil
discussed with Rep. Pagdilao what particular steps can be undertaken by the MILF to restore peace in Mindanao and for the Bangsamoro Basic Law to succeed. Reps. Bataoil and Pagdilao also discussed what the government could do for the fallen troopers and their families, and the need for Congress to establish clearer procedures or protocol so that such situations will not be repeated. Rep. Bataoil then suggested that the Members should pass the hat so they could immediately help the bereaved families of the slain SAF forces. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.41,p.5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2015-01-28
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Bataoil. Referred to the Cttee. Rules.

rows.author: G093;
rows.title_full: DEATH OF P N P - S A F TROOPS I MAMASAPANO, MAGUINDANAO
rows.title_short: Killing Of S A F In Mamasapano
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Tinio first condoled
with the bereaved families of the members of the
Philippine National Police-Special Action Force
(PNP-SAF) who were killed in an incident involving the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) in Mamapasano, Maguindanao. He then centered his speech on the government authorities responsible for the SAF operation in the area, noting the press statement of Secretary Manuel A. Roxas II of the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) that he and the PNP officer-in-charge were not informed of said operation and thus it was
conducted without any clearance from them.
Expressing his disbelief that the operation was
unauthorized, he stressed that the DILG secretary and PNP chief are both under the President, and for which reason Congress should inquire into the latter´s role in the SAF incident. Thereafter, Rep. Tinio cited facts pointing to the possible involvement of the United States´ Joint Special Operations Task Force in the Mamapasano incident, and urged Congress to investigate the extent of the US government´s participation therein.
(Continuation)
After citing a newspaper report alleging that the
President authorized the SAF operation with the
involvement of suspended PNP Chief Alan Purisima,
Rep. Tinio then called for an inquiry into the
accountability of the President in the Mamapasano
incident. On motion of Rep. Bondoc, the Chair recognized Rep. Jose L. Atienza Jr. for his manifestation.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Rep. Atienza requested his colleagues to join
hands in expressing sentiments of indignation and
concern over the Mamapasano incident that resulted in the death of numerous SAF members and for Congress to stop temporarily the public hearings on the proposed Bangsamoro Basic Law (BBL).
REMARKS OF THE CHAIR
The Chair remarked that his manifestation was
well taken and that it is up to the Ad Hoc Committee on the BBL whether or not to postpone the liberations on the BBL.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.42
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2015-01-28
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Rep.Atienza

rows.author: C032;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Cerilles expressed grief over the recent
deaths of the 44 PNP-SAF personnel. She averred that the incident was a massacre rather than a misencounter and articulated that the government´s adoption of the MILF´s pronouncement that what happened was a misencounter was irresponsible. She noted that the MILF washed its hands and pointed a finger to the Bangsamoro Islamic Freedom Fighters (BIFF) as the perpetrators and that the MILF merely fought back the PNPSAF men in self defense. She opined that the PNPSAF must have been withdrawing, knowing that they already got Zulkifli Bin Hir alias Marwan, one of the
two international terrorists they were after. With the bloody incident, she said that several questions arose leaving the Members hanging on whether to suspend or continue with the proposed Bangsamoro Basic Law (BBL). As she questioned the rush for the approval of the BBL and the sincerity of the MILF, Rep. Cerilles then
moved that the House suspend its deliberations while the investigation on the incident was ongoing and until the MILF was found innocent of the deaths of the members of the SAF.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.43,p.1)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-02
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G002;
rows.title_full: DEATH OF PNP-SAF TROOPS IN MAMASAPANO, MAGUINDANAO
rows.abstract:
Rep. Acop paid tribute to the fallen heroes of the PNP-SAF now known as the “Fallen 44” and acknowledged the sacrifice not only of these men but also of others who had died in similar circumstances. He stressed that despite what happened, the country should continue to pursue the long and arduous process of peace because doing otherwise would result only in more killings. Condemning nevertheless what he called a ghastly act and demanding justice for the
dead, he asked the MILF to determine who were responsible for the killings so that they could be brought to trial; return and account for the looted personal possessions and equipment from the SAF victims; explain why the two aforecited terrorists lived in their stronghold areas; and state what its exact status with the BIFF was.
As he discussed the barometer for the achievement
of peace and the peace efforts of both the government and the MILF, he strongly urged both sides to form an independent panel that would investigate the unfortunate incident to identify the lapses and determine the accountability of those responsible without partiality and prejudice. In conclusion, Rep. Acop gave his respects and gratitude to the “Fallen 44” for what they have offered in the name of peace.
Thereafter, on motion of Rep. Defensor, the Chair
recognized Rep. Walden F. Bello for his interpellation.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BELLO (W.)
At the outset, Reps. Bello and Acop discussed the
composition of the members of the soon-to-be formed PNP Board of Inquiry that would delve into the issue and the participation of civil society groups in such panel; the status of the deliberations on the Bangsamoro Basic Law in which the former expressed support for the continuation of the same; and the possible
involvement of the United States in the operation of the SAF. With Rep. Bello expressing concern about the US involvement in the incident, and the desire for the conduct of an investigation on the MILF behavior, government
accountability, lack of coordination between
the SAF and the Armed Forces of the Philippines for the rescue of the commandos, Rep. Acop agreed to an inquiry on the matter as well as a review of the statement made by the government.
Finally, Rep. Acop referred to Article II of the
Peace Agreement insofar as the need for coordination among the parties involved is concerned, as well as for the handling and involvement of such an operation by the topmost level of government.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. PAGDILAO
Recognized by the Chair, on motion of Rep. Defensor, Rep. Samuel D. Pagdilao discussed with Rep. Acop how justice for the massacred members of the PNP-SAF could be achieved, with the latter expressing hope that an investigation could be made to determine and punish the accountable parties. They also dwelled on the formation of an independent investigative body,
the summoning of the individuals concerned, and the conduct of a trial to come out with the truth. The two Members also agreed that justice for the grieving families should be served first before the deliberation of the BBL.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.43,pp.1-2)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2015-02-03
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Bello(W.) and Pagdilao. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G025;
rows.title_full: DEATH OF PNP-SAF TROOPS IN MAMASAPANO, MAGUINDANAO
rows.abstract:
Rep. Cojuangco spoke about the sentiments of a
PNP-SAF member concerning the conflicting accounts on the death of the 44 police commandos in Mamasapano, Maguindanao on January 25 stating that the PNP-SAF commandos were surrounded and attacked by the combined forces of the MILF and BIFF while serving the warrant of arrest to Marwan and Usman. After citing all the conflicting accounts on the incident, she saw the need for the government to: 1) identify who gave the clearance to the operation to determine
who is accountable using the principle of command
responsibility; 2) proceed to its honest to goodness investigation; and 3) review and revise or trash the BBL. She also brought to the fore her concerns as a Member of the 16th Congress to set aside all legalities and semantics since the massacre is about heart, soul, hurt feelings and distrust; and thereafter reiterated her call not to continue with the discussions on the BBL
because doing so would be very callous on the part of the 16th Congress. (SOURCE: House Journal No.43,p.2)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2015-02-03
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F122;
rows.title_full: REITERATING THE CALL FOR A HOUSE INVESTIGATION ON THE DEATHS OF PNP-SAF TROOPS IN MAMASAPANO, MAGUINDANAO
rows.title_short: Postponement Of The Discussion Of The B B L In View Of The Fallen 44
rows.abstract:
Rep. Dela Cruz initially stated that last January 27, 2015, he stood before the Body and urged the Members to act as one to honor the dead and get to the bottom of the tragic incident. He proposed that Congress authorize the creation of an independent commission
not only to investigate the conduct of Operation Wolverine and the developments thereafter but to ascertain the impact of the undertaking on the overall security situation and the entire peace process and other initiatives on the Moro issue which then, he said, means a review of the 1976 Tripoli Agreement and the 1996 Jakarta Accord. However, while the Speaker had acceded to his proposals including said creation of an independent commission, Rep. Dela Cruz said that he was surprised when the Speaker is now being quoted that he will not support any inquiry on the Mamasapano massacre until after the Board of Inquiry created by the DILG/PNP shall have issued its own report on the matter. Rep. Dela Cruz expressed hope that the Speaker had only been misquoted or taken out of context and urged the latter to reconsider his position if it were so. Thereafter, Rep. Dela Cruz inquired on the recent allotment of P8.5 billion to the Autonomous Region, the reason for which is still questionable. He then urged the House leadership to listen to concerned citizens and ensure that they do not enter in accord which may cost countless of lives all over again and crush the
dreams and aspirations for just and lasting peace. In closing his speech, Rep. Dela Cruz read into the record some passages from the writings of Mr. Teddy Boy Locsin and Father Ranhilio Aquino.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. MAGSAYSAY
Reps. Dela Cruz and Magsaysay then discussed
the derailment of the passage of the BBL and urged the House leadership to heed the proposal of several Members for a resolution suspending the deliberations thereon until the Board of Inquiry comes up with a report. (SOURCE: House Journal No.43,pp.2-3)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2015-02-03
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Magsaysay. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H017;
rows.title_full: HONORING THE HEROISM OF ALL PNP-SAF TROOPS INVOLVED IN OPLAN WOLVERINE
rows.abstract:
Rep. Belmonte expressed the solidarity of the
House of Representatives and his and the Chamber´s sentiment about an incident that has tested the government´s and the nation´s resolve to end the Mindanao conflict and achieve lasting peace, protect the people from terrorism and violence, and secure justice for all. Saying they could not have peace and justice at the expense of the other, he also expressed outrage at the fact that members of the SAF had to die and that their families had to suffer in order to fulfill a mission to protect the people from terrorists. He enumerated the names of the “Fallen 44” and called them as well as their
wounded comrades, as heroes. Rep. Belmonte then asked his colleagues to join him in silence to thank the policemen and God for keeping the country safe and to send the message that they are ready to pay any price for peace and order.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.43,pp.3-4)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2015-02-03
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules on Feb.03,2015.

rows.author: H081;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Zarate raised the issue of rights violations
and redress of grievances of political prisoners in the country. He cited a hunger strike recently held by inmates in Camp Bagong Diwa whose jail warden disallowed them from seeing their doctors, lawyers and families and sowed intrigue among their groups or gangs. He said that many prisoners have not yet been convicted of any crime. In view that most of the political prisoners were consultants of the National Democratic Front, he proposed the resumption of peace talks between the Government of the Philippines and the National Democratic Front to address the root causes of armed rebellion and the perpetuating political and economic disparity in the country. (SOURCE: House Journal No.44,p.8)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-03
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G012;
rows.title_short: Medal Of Valor For S A F 44
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bataoil proposed that the Medal of Valor or
the Medalya ng Kagitingan be awarded to the 44
members of the Special Action Force who died in the Mamasapano incident instead of the Medal of Bravery or the Medalya ng Katapangan already given them. He pointed out that the SAF members´ gallantry at the risk of their lives and against a superior number of enemies is in accordance with the provisions for such an award under Presidential Decree No 1687. He added that
Republic Act No. 9049 also grants awardees thereof to a lifetime gratuity of â‚±20,000. Stressing that the award will boost the morale
of the PNP, he urged the Body to act accordingly.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.44,p.8)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-03
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F100;
rows.abstract:
Upon motion of Rep. Defensor, the Chair recognized Rep. Neri J. Colmenares from Bayan Muna Party-List who spoke about the unfulfilled promise of clean and automated elections in 2010 and 2013 because of lack of safeguards in the use of precinct count optical scanner (PCOS) machines; the absence of means of verifying the votes; and the Commission on Elections´(Comelec) use of the services of two foreign companies, Smartmatic and Dominion, in the counting of votes. He showed how the PCOS system introduced a foreign-dominated method that violates the principles of secret voting and public counting and does not give the people the chance to object and oppose questionable results, which is a violation of their right to suffrage. He proposed the use of a better alternative called
the Automated Canvassing Election System (ACES)
that employs manual counting of votes at the precinct level but uses automation at the canvassing level and addresses the problems on verification and validation of canvass results. He added that the ACES parts and computers are locally available and the Board of Election
Inspectors (BEIs) can easily learn the system
without experiencing the same problems encountered with the PCOS. Rep. Colmenares underscored the importance of the 2016 presidential elections and the chaos it will
bring in the country if the same election breakdown and lack of credibility will happen again. He said that changing the PCOS system now is imperative if the people were to effectively exercise their right to suffrage.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.45,pp.5-6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-04
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G093;
rows.title_short: Commemoration Of The 116th Year Of Fil - Am War
rows.abstract:
Rep.Tinio spoke about the 116th anniversary of the Philippine-American War, recalling the struggles of Filipino soldiers against US imperialism that showed the Filipinos´ burning and defiant patriotism to fight for independence despite the overwhelming odds which is true until this day. He then recalled the incidents of atrocities and barbarity allegedly committed
by the Americans during the occupation. Rep. Tinio said that he had filed two measures: 1)
House Resolution No.130, demanding an apology
from the US government, stressing the urgency and
necessity for such acknowledgment in relation to the Aquino administration´s initiatives to expand the presence of US military forces and facilities on Philippine soil; and 2) House Bill No.448, declaring February 4 as a special working holiday to commemorate the Philippine-American War Day in honor of the patriotism
and self-sacrifice of Filipino heroes who fought
American aggression. Lastly, he observed that American imperialism still persists and establishes itself in the name of political, military, economic positioning and domination through the Enhanced Defense Cooperation
Agreement and in the Mamasapano operation.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.45,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-04
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H065;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Atienza spoke about the enactment of the
Reproductive Health Law which, in his opinion, ran counter to a proclamation signed by the late President Corazon C. Aquino, respecting life from birth to death, as well as the constitutional provision mandating the
protection of life in all its form. He reminded his colleagues that the country might not have produced national heroes had it adhered to the policy of birth control in eradicating poverty.
In light thereof, Rep. Atienza said that he had filed a bill repealing the Reproductive Health Law and called upon the Members to stand up for what is right. He likewise urged them to review and scrutinize the measures being deliberated upon or are pending in the House which will not protect the life of the unborn and not promote the family as the foundation of the society.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BAGATSING
On motion of Rep. Ortega (F.), the Chair
recognized Rep. Amado S. Bagatsing who initially
congratulated Rep. Atienza on his position regarding the Reproductive Health Law. He then discussed with him his concern on whether the Philippines would have a more favorable economic ratings given by the Standard and Poor´s and Moodys if not for the country´s overpopulation.
At this juncture, Deputy Speaker Apostol
relinquished the Chair to Rep. Jorge “Bolet” Banal. On further issues that had been raised in the interpellation, Rep. Atienza emphasized the
importance of a burgeoning population to attain a
substantial number of workforce that can contribute to a growing and progressive economy, citing the case of the Philippines with its economic progress being supported by its 10 million migrant workers abroad who contribute about $40 billion annually to the domestic economy. In his rejoinder, Rep. Bagatsing underscored the priorities that government must need to address to govern an increasing population, specifically in the areas of education and health. He argued that the lives
of the majority of the poor Filipinos would be served well if only the pertinent government agencies would undertake crucial measures in protecting the health and providing for the education of the youth. On motion of Rep. Monique Yazmin Q. Lagdameo, the Chair recognized Rep. Jonathan A.Dela Cruz for his interpellation.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Rep. Dela Cruz sought clarification on several
issues pertaining specifically to the impact of the increasing number of the Filipino population to economic development. He argued on the beneficial advantages of an increasing population, as can be gleaned from countries trying to propagate their aged population and workforce, and which he said are conducive to young economies like the Philippines to attain economic growth. Rep. Atienza agreed therewith and claimed that inequitable distribution of economic wealth actually hampers an increasing, productive population. To address such adverse situation, he proposed that Philippine government focus its economic and poverty
alleviation programs towards managing the country´s increasing population, ensuring the wide allocation of economic wealth and resources to all sectors of the Philippine economy, and protecting the natural resources and food supply of the country.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.46,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-09
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps.Bagatsing and Dela Cruz. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: B006;
rows.title_short: Resumption Of Consideration Of Bangsa Moro Basic Law
rows.abstract:
In his speech, Deputy Speaker Balindong stated
that as he supports President Benigno S. Aquino III in his call for peace in the country, and in light of what happened in Mamasapano, Maguindanao, he was persuaded to push for the urgent passage of the proposed Bangsamoro Basic Law (BBL). He expressed belief that the BBL is the political solution to the secessionist struggle of the Bangsamoro people. He further said that instead of antipathy, the House
leadership should resume consideration of said
measure.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.47,p.4)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2015-02-10)
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G101;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Yap spoke about the ongoing Senate and
House hearings on the Mamasapano massacre which
revealed mistakes and led to finger-pointing that was painful for the Filipino nation to endure. For all the parties involved to be able to rebuild trust and goodwill, he urged the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) to surrender the perpetrators to the police authorities; the national government to go back to the negotiating table to demand justice from the MILF; the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) and the Philippine National Police (PNP) not to engage in any act of atrocity and retribution in Mindanao; and Congress to resume the deliberations on the proposed
Bangsamoro Basic Law.
