(SOURCE: House Journal No.49,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-16
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G105;
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Bondoc, the Chair recognized
Rep. Emmi A. De Jesus of Gabriela Party-List who
spoke in Filipino about the issue of economic violence against women in the form of labor contractualization in light of the government´s policies on economic liberalization and globalization. She said that nationalist industrialization is the real solution to the problem of unemployment and urged the Members to
approve more measures providing enough incentives
and care and health benefits for women workers as
well as to approve the bill imposing a decent minimum wage level for all workers in the country. Lastly, she invited the Members to the celebration of the International Women´s Day on March 8. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.49,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-16
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G057;
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Bondoc, the Chair recognized
Rep. Tupay T. Loong from the First District of Sulu who raised several concerns regarding government´s efforts to establish the truth in several of its investigations on the massacre of the 44 members of the PNP-Special Action Force (SAF). In particular, he argued that the inquiry being undertaken by the PNP through the Board of Inquiry and the investigation by Congress on the massacre must take into account the unnecessary deaths of the MILF members and the innocent civilians, both of whom, he said, had not
initiated the gun battle with the PNP-SAF. He appealed for peace and sobriety and further asked those clamoring for an all-out war against the MILF and secessionist Muslim Filipinos to rethink their position, prejudices, and biases against the Muslim Filipinos most of whom, he said, were predominantly in favor of the resumption of the peace process with the government and the enactment into law of the Bangsamoro Basic Law.
Rep. Loong maintained that every Filipino must
consider the consequences of deterrence to any effort for peace and reconciliation considering that Muslim Filipinos had gravely suffered through repeated wars and atrocities committed against them by the Philippine government, which have resulted in thousands of deaths, destroyed lives and properties, and caused permanent social, psychological, emotional, and economic harm to Muslim Filipinos. He stressed that their Muslim brothers do not want to return to war just to defend their lives and territories. 
(House Journal No.49,p.7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-16
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G086;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Sema strongly deplored the anti-Muslim
Filipino sentiment prevailing in the country and in the media circles pertaining to the alleged massacre of 44 PNP-SAF members in Mamasapano, Maguindanao. She argued that the alleged massacre had caused so much anger among non-Muslim Filipinos that it had also caused prejudicial consequences to the deliberation of the draft Bangsamoro Basic Law and to peace in Mindanao.
She opined that the ongoing government investigation on the Mamasapano incident that had
consequently resulted to adverse public opinion
against Muslim Filipinos would be a preview to
jeopardizing the Bangsamoro Basic Law. She
explained that even the deaths of countless civilians who were merely treated as collateral damage of the war were not taken cognizance in the investigation. She hoped that peace would still be a reality between the Philippine government and the MILF, the Bangsamoro Islamic Freedom Fighters (BIFF) and similar armed groups in Mindanao, especially since wars and threats of war from the Philippine government had adversely affected the lives of Muslim Filipinos since the 1970s. In ending her speech, Rep. Sema asked the people
to pray for her and the country´s leaders that peace would reign in their words, their deeds and especially in their hearts. 
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BELLO (W.)
Reps. Bello and Sema discussed the ongoing Senate investigation with the former expressing his
belief that the Senate´s inquiry is being done to achieve something other than finding the truth with regard to the Mamasapano incident. In ending his interpellation, Rep. Bello likewise expressed that he is one with Reps. Loong and Sema in their concern about getting into the heart of the matter and making sure that the Bangsamoro people´s history is not distorted at the expense of other vested interests. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.49,pp.7-8)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-16
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep.Bello(W.). Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F122;
rows.abstract:
In his speech, Rep. Dela Cruz expressed his
sentiments on the postponement of the Committee´s
hearing on the Mamasapano incident the next day. He observed that judging from the recent developments, it was clear that there are elaborate and insidious efforts on the part of the highest officials of the land, particularly those in the Executive Branch, to muddle issues in a misplaced attempt to escape responsibility over the killing of the 44 SAF members. Likewise, he
observed that the officials were trying to shield the President from any responsibility when he himself already revealed interesting facts about his role and the information he was receiving during his sessions with the SAF on January 25. He underscored that they should raise their voices against any and all attempts to let the tragedy become a farce and the perpetrators of the dastardly act go scot-free. Thereupon, Rep. Dela Cruz explained that the Members who participated in said hearing merely wanted to uncover the truth. He said that if Congress could not accomplish this mission, the government should establish an independent truth commission.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Reps. Atienza and Dela Cruz discussed the lack of
transparency, credibility, truthfulness, accountability, and leadership among the President, his officials, and military/police authorities. Rep. Dela Cruz reiterated that if Congress itself could not ferret out the truth, an
independent truth commission should be able to do so. As he expressed support to the decision of the
House leadership to postpone the Committee hearings on the Mamasapano tragedy because of the different political intentions of the Members, Rep. Atienza supported the call of Rep. Dela Cruz for the creation of an independent truth commission composed of nonpartisan and nonpolitical personalities that would handle the investigation and ferret out the truth and give justice to the sacrifices made by the 44 SAF
members.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ERICE
Reps. Dela Cruz and Erice focused their discussion on whether Congress should wait for the results of the investigation on the Mamasapano tragedy being conducted by the PNP Board of Inquiry. Considering that the Executive Department, as well as the PNP and the AFP, has been very cooperative in the
deliberations being conducted by both Houses of
Congress, Rep. Erice enjoined his colleagues not to prejudge the result of the inquiry and to trust its veracity. For his part, Rep. Dela Cruz pointed out however that there is lack of transparency, credibility, truthfulness and accountability among the President, his cabinet officials as well as the military and police authorities as they have given inconsistent and conflicting statements on the issue. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.49,pp.8-9)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2016-02-16)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Atienza and Erice. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F100;
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep.
Bondoc, Rep. Neri J. Colmenares of Bayan Muna
Party-List expressed concern that the House might fail to fulfill its investigative functions over the Mamasapano incident. He stressed the need to clarify the President as well as the United States´ role therein, particularly the allegation that the former allowed himself to be dictated upon by the latter. With the information that no hearings would be conducted by the Committee on Public Order and Safety on February 17 and 18, 2015, he underscored that the House should perform its mandate of pursuing said meetings to find out the truth and hold the guilty parties accountable.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.49,p.9)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-16
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G093;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Tinio joined Rep. Colmenares in condemning
the decision of the House to cancel the scheduled
hearings on the Mamasapano encounter, this as he
noted the unfinished issue about the alleged meeting between President Aquino and former PNP Chief Alan Purisima, as well as the newspaper reports about the US government´s involvement in Oplan Exodus. He underscored the Congress´ obligation to find out the truth, and lamented that the discontinuance of the Committee hearings would only benefit the President. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.49,p.10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-16
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F102;
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Bondoc, the Chair recognized
Rep. Bello who expressed apprehension on the
cancellation of the hearings of the Committee on
Public Order and Safety on the Mamasapano incident, reasoning out that it might be construed as an abdication of the House oversight function over the Executive and might create suspicion among the majority of the people that there was an effort to block the truth on the real culprit behind the failed operation. He also pointed out that a deeper investigation on the role of the United States special force on the matter has
to be clarified. He then expressed his support to the Members who would like to continue the hearings and appealed to the House leadership to reverse its decision on the postponement of the joint Committee hearings set for the next two days. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.49,p.10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-16
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H029;
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep. Bondoc, Rep. Gwendolyn F. Garcia also spoke about the postponement of the hearings on the Mamasapano
incident to be conducted by the Committee on Public Order and Safety, and the Special Committee on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity. She recalled that she had manifested a motion to set additional hearings on Tuesday and Wednesday because it was important to ferret out the truth on the incident and that the two resource persons, Secretaries Mar Roxas and Voltaire Gazmin, had other pressing matters to attend to that day and as such her motion was to serve as notice for the two resource speakers so that they would be able to fix their schedules accordingly. She said that although there was a Board of Inquiry that would conduct an investigation, she stressed it was incumbent upon them, Representatives of the people, to conduct their own investigation so that all the questions of their constituents would be heard and answered. She expressed disappointment on the sudden postponement of the hearings until further notice that may raise suspicion among the public. She
then appealed to the Chairpersons of the two
Committees concerned to reconsider their decisions.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. LOBREGAT
On motion of Rep. Bondoc, the Chair recognized
Rep. Celso L. Lobregat who discussed with Rep.
Garcia (G.) his concerns on whether the latter was the one who had earlier moved to reschedule the
Committee hearings for February 17 and 18; and on
whether she has knowledge on how the two
chairpersons have arrived at the decision to postpone the hearings. Rep. Lobregat discussed the reason and lack of justification for the indefinite postponement of the Committee hearings on the Mamasapano incident. He opined that the House of Representatives could be at the end of adverse public opinion more particularly since the Senate is presumed to be continuing with its
investigations as it had already completed three public hearings and two executive sessions on the incident. He added that the postponement of the Housei investigations would deprive their respective constituencies of representative participation in the Committee hearings. He surmised that the hearings were postponed presumably because the Committees could be awaiting the results of the investigation of the
PNP Board of Inquiry. In her reply, Rep. Garcia maintained that there are no lawful and valid justifications for the arbitrary and unilateral decision by the chairpersons of the two Committees to postpone the congressional hearings indefinitely and concurred that this decision should be arrived at through a consensus of the majority of the Committee members. She agreed that the House will be adversely affected by this decision in view of suspicions of conspiracy to withhold the facts and vital information about the case from the public. In reiterating the need for the House to resume its congressional hearings on the Mamasapano incident, she concurred with the appeal of Rep. Lobregat to the chairpersons of the two Committees to reconsider their action on coming up with a notice of indefinite postponement of the congressional inquiries. 
INTERPELLATION OF REP. TAMBUNTING
Rep. Tambunting initially sought Rep. Garcia´s
(G.) concurrence with regard to the particular events and circumstances of the Committee hearings adverted to in the interpellation, including among others: the request of some of the Committee Members during its last hearing on the Mamasapano incident to extend the same but which was overruled by the majority of the Members supporting the decision of the Committee chair to terminate the hearing at four-thirty in the
afternoon so they can attend the plenary session but with the understanding that the inquiry will resume on Tuesday, February 17; and the fact that the Committee hearings had been productive considering that certain matters regarding the killing of the 44 SAF members had been made known to the public. In ending his interpellation, Rep. Tambunting joined the Members who spoke before him in their appeal to reconsider the decision to suspend indefinitely the hearings on the Mamasapano incident because in doing so, they would be remiss of their duty. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.49,pp.10
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2015-02-16)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Lobregat and Tambunting. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F102;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bello said that recent hearings of the Committee on Public Order and Safety and the Special Committee on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity revealed that it was the lack of communication among the President, military and police authorities, and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) in arresting an
international terrorist that led to the so-called Mamasapano Massacre. He stressed that the congressional hearings should go on, in order to uncover more evidence to support the suspicion that the United States participated in planning and implementing the operation. He stressed that Congress has to perform its oversight function and not leave the investigation to the Executive as this might only lead to a coverup of the issue.
As he opined that the Mamasapano tragedy has
destabilized the peace process, Rep. Bello urged his colleagues not to turn their backs on the deliberation of the draft Bangsamoro Basic Law (BBL) and to ignore personalities that saw said tragedy as a way to further one´s political agenda as clearly demonstrated in the Senate hearings the previous week. As such, Rep. Bello appealed 1) to the Members to promote sobriety in the search for truth and peaceful settlement of the Mindanao conflict; 2) to the Senator in question to desist from poisonous rhetoric and cease using the Senate hearing in the Mamasapano tragedy as a platform for his political ambition; and 3) to President
Benigno S. Aquino III to fully accept responsibility for the Mamasapano fiasco and disclose the participation of the United States in the police operation. In conclusion, Rep. Bello urged the House leadership to continue with the investigation of the Mamasapano tragedy.
Thereafter, on motion of Rep. Bondoc, the Chair
recognized Rep. Jonathan A. Dela Cruz for his interpellation. 
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Reps. Bello (W.) and Dela Cruz affirmed that
Congress should continue with its inquiry into the Mamasapano tragedy particularly on the participation of the United States in the operation of the Philippine National Police (PNP)-Special Action Force (SAF) and the order for the Armed Forces of the Philippines to stand down. Both Members agreed that the PNP Board of Inquiry has a limited forum considering that it would only be limited to the operational aspect of the
issue and that there are a number of points that should be answered considering the conflicting and inconsistent statements and lack of transparency, credibility, truthfulness and accountability of military and police officials. While both agreed that it is the duty of the Members to know the truth about the Mamasapano incident given the Congress´ oversight functions over the actions
of Malacañang, they also dwelled on the failure
of the present Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM) and the need for the Committee on Public Order and Safety and the Special Committee on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity to continue with their joint inquiry so its findings could be used by the Ad Hoc Committee on the BBL in its deliberation on the national security provisions of the draft BBL. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.50,p.5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-17
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Dela Cruz. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F012;
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep. Bondoc,
Rep. Elpidio F. Barzaga Jr. from the Fourth District of Cavite spoke about the various news reports regarding the arrest of his alleged grandson by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) for using shabu last Friday, February 13, 2015 inside the Barzaga compound in Dasmariñas City, Cavite. He cited details to show that the accused is not and cannot be his grandson,
does not live in Dasmarinas City, and has Gatuz
as his last name. He added that his name was mentioned in the news reports apparently to sensationalize the incident. In the interest of justice and fair play, Rep. Barzaga said that he had to stand up on behalf of all public officials whose names might be greatly damaged by the abuse of press freedom, especially with the conduct
of the forthcoming local elections in 2016. He
suggested that an investigation be conducted by the Body in order for the NBI to exercise due care and diligence in releasing reports. In light thereof, he moved that his speech be referred
to the Committees on Public Information, and
Justice so that appropriate investigation in aid of legislation could be made. With the indulgence of his colleagues, he said that he would not entertain any interpellation.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.50,pp.5-6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-17
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: H072;
rows.abstract:
Terry L. Ridon of Kabataan Party-List who denounced the move of the House leadership on the abrupt cancellation of the congressional investigation on the Mamasapano operation for the following reasons: it comes at a time when the main players in the operation, particularly former PNP Chief Alan Purisima, are about to answer questions essential to the pursuit of truth and accountability; it is an unjustifiable suppression
of the right of each and every Member of the House to participate and be heard; and it comes at a
time when a most pressing issue needs to be discussed which is the involvement of the United States in the whole Mamasapano affair. Rep. Ridon´s contentions against the unilateral
and arbitrary decision of the House leadership and the Committee chairpersons to postpone the congressional hearings indefinitely underscored the following: a) there are no lawful and justifiable reasons for the House leadership and the Committee chairpersons to postpone indefinitely the congressional hearings that concern national interest and national security; b)this is averse to the prevailing public opinion for the House to continue with its investigation; c) this is contrary to determining the facts of the alleged massacre of the 44 PNP-SAF, specifically exculpating officials in public office of their imprimatur and political participation allowing the PNP-SAF to proceed with their police operations in Mamasapano; d) this is not in accordance with the mandate of the Representatives of the people; and e) this is an outright suppression of the right to information of the people. 
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Rep. Atienza inquired from Rep. Ridon the possible
courses of action of the majority of the Members
so they can express their sentiment for the continuation
and resumption of the House investigation on the
Mamasapano incident. He explained that the decision of the House leadership and the Committee chairpersons to postpone the hearings had put the House in an adverse political situation more so that the officials of the PNoy Administration had not been forthcoming in their answers during the congressional investigation and “caught lying” regarding the facts of the incident. He then asked whether Rep. Ridon would agree to a Resolution to elicit the sentiment of the majority regarding
the continuation of congressional hearings on
the death of the 44 PNP-SAF members. Rep. Ridon concurred with the proposed Resolution and stated that the arbitrary and unilateral action of the House leadership and the Committee chairpersons
to postpone the congressional hearings indefinitely should also be put to a vote in the plenary.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.50,p.6)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2015-02-17)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep.Atienza.

rows.author: F093;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ilagan took the floor to add the women´s
voice to the clamor for truth and accountability on the Mamasapano incident, and for the House to resume its hearings thereon. She related the personal information she had gathered when she joined a fact-finding mission conducted in the area from February 8 to 11, 2015. After concluding that the narratives she heard during the said mission were totally different from the testimonies made during the official investigations, she relayed the people´s desire for an impartial investigation and the punishment of guilty officials.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.52,p.16)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-23
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: F122;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Dela Cruz called the attention of the Body
to the sad state of Camp John Hay which was heralded two decades ago as the centerpiece of Baguio City´s resurgence as the tourism and commercial hub of Northern Luzon. He illustrated how the highhanded management style of the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) President Arnel Paciano Casanova against its private partner - the Sobrepeña Group - has resulted in a failed public private partnership (PPP) undertaking. In order to achieve the original purpose and vision of the PPP projects, Rep. Dela Cruz asked the Members to legislate the following measures that will ensure that the Camp John Hay Project and other PPP undertakings will be insulated from the capricious and high-handed practices of the heads of agencies who are tasked to implement such developmental undertakings: 1) provide better and expedient dispute resolution mechanisms so that the PPP partners are not left at the mercy of an oppressive agency partner; and 2) create an oversight committee for PPP projects
which should include not only the officials of the implementing agency but also the reputable members of the private sector.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ALIPING
On motion of Rep. Durano, the Chair recognized
Rep. Nicasio M. Aliping Jr. who discussed with Rep. Dela Cruz his concerns on the other recourse that the Baguio City government can do to collect its 25 percent share of rental revenues in Camp John Hay; whether the House Special Committee on Bases Conversion can conduct an inquiry in aid of legislation, directing the BCDA and the Camp John Hay Development Corporation (CJHDevCo) to pay Baguio City said revenue share; and the legal remedies available to the parties in the arbitration process. He surmised that the city will be prejudiced if it will not be able to
reiterate its legal right to a 25 percent share in the rental revenues. Rep. Dela Cruz agreed therewith and explained that one legal recourse for the city government is to insist that the rental payments be put in a trust fund to be administered by the Department of Finance of
which the 25 percent legally accruing to Baguio City will be sourced from. 
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ERICE
Rep. Erice sought the clarification of Rep. Dela
Cruz regarding the involvement of the Sobrepeña
Group with the BCDA in Camp John Hay and inquired
whether this is the same Group involved in
several government infrastructure projects such as the MRT-3. He proposed that the issues raised by Rep. Dela Cruz on the claims of the City of Baguio should also include an investigation of the Sobrepeña Group to determine its alleged liabilities with the government. Rep. Dela Cruz informed Rep. Erice that the parties in this case were obliged by the Court to pursue arbitration process. He thereafter commended Rep. Erice for taking cognizance of the issue involving the
Sobrepeña Group and its alleged anomalous involvement with government infrastructure projects under the Ramos Administration and the subsequent administrations. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.54,pp.3-4)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-25
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Aliping and Erice. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H065;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Atienza raised his contentions and utmost
concern regarding the apparent disinterest and official disregard of the celebration of EDSA People Power Revolution or EDSA I, specifically resulting from the misplaced notion of certain sectors of the society that there had not been any substantial and effective changes in the country´s political, economic, and sociocultural milieu after EDSA I. Rep. Atienza thereafter enumerated the conditions prevalent in the country prior to EDSA I, specifically during the alleged authoritarian Marcos regime, and argued that contrary to the misplaced notion, EDSA I had brought about substantial reforms politically and economically and allowed the Filipinos for the first time, a system of government under a
duly elected democracy. Even as the governments
after EDSA I up to the present have not yet fully alleviated the adverse political, economic, and sociocultural conditions in the country, he noted that the PNoy Administration has been sensitive in addressing the plight of poor Filipinos. Thus, he disagreed with the call of certain sectors for the resignation of President Benigno S. Aquino III, a military intervention, and a return to martial rule, stating that this is inimical to the interest of the country. He stressed a true
government of the people should be sensitive to the needs of the people and should exude such sensitivity in all levels of public office and governance. In light of the day´s commemoration of EDSA I, Rep. Atienza expressed disappointment that the government only proclaimed the day as a nonschooling day. He said that the government should not disregard what happened in EDSA in 1986 because this was the time when the people succeeded in their struggle for freedom.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
To Rep. Dela Cruz´ queries, Rep. Atienza replied
that he had mixed emotions in commemorating
EDSA I because it seemed that some people do not
know the full meaning of a people power revolution. He said that in fact, people power revolution should be taught in school so that younger generations would know its true meaning.
On Rep. Dela Cruz´ other concerns, Rep. Atienza
underscored the differences between the Regular Batasang Pambansa and the present Congress, including, among others: the Members´ attitude in attending the daily sessions, how Members give importance to their roles as elected officials, how bills are crafted, and how Members are given freedom to speak on the floor on whatever issue they want to speak about. Rep. Atienza likewise recalled when the Opposition Members walked out of the same Session Hall after being maligned for protesting the proclamation of the late President Ferdinand E. Marcos as the winner in the 1986 snap presidential elections. Rep. Atienza also stressed that the legislators should review the proposed Bangsamoro Basic Law (BBL) with an impartial, nonpartisan, and nonpolitical point of view. On resuming hearings thereon, he said that the entire Body should decide; the Members should explain their positions; and that he would file the pertinent Resolution the following week. Rep. Dela Cruz expressed support for his colleague´s views as he asked the House to heed the public clamor for truth and justice regarding the Mamasapano
incident.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.54,pp.4-5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-02-25
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep.dela Cruz. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H046;
rows.abstract:
Initially, Rep. Olivarez stated that February 13,
2015 was the 17th anniversary of the cityhood of
Parañaque and gave a background of its origins and

He also discussed the different strategies being employed as well as the projects and programs being implemented under the administration of incumbent Mayor Edwin Olivarez to bring about good local governance in the city. rows.author: C403;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Biazon spoke about the various peace
initiatives tried by the Philippine government
beginning with the administration of the late Pres. Ferdinand E. Marcos until the present, to achieve peace in Mindanao. He said that the most recent of these is the comprehensive framework agreement with the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) that produced the Bangsamoro Basic Law (BBL) which the Members are expected to support and ensure that it will bring about lasting peace in the region. He underscored that the Mindanao conflict has caused the deaths of hundreds of thousands of Filipinos, wastage of billions of pesos, weakening of Mindanao´s economy, and the bleeding of the national economy in general. He pointed out that the pending draft BBL is envisioned to put a stop to all of these but that the Members have to reconcile the interests of the different stakeholders; ensure that the BBL receives majority support despite the broken
trust among the parties involved which the
Mamasapano incident has caused; and make sure that
the enactment of the proposed measure will pass
constitutional scrutiny.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.55,pp.7-8,12-14)

rows.remarks: Interpellation by Dep.Spkr. Balindong, Bagatsing, Loong, Atienza, Dela Cruz and Lobregat. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F012;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Barzaga spoke on the disqualification made
by the bids and awards committee (BAC) of the
Commission on Elections (Comelec) on the
prospective bidders, namely Smartmatic and Indra
Sistemas, for the lease with option to purchase
additional precinct count optical scan (PCOS)
machines and other necessary equipment to be used in the automated May 2016 elections. Citing the reasons of the BAC for disqualifying the two bidders, he stated that the Comelec had pronounced that on account of said disqualification, their preparations for the coming 2016 elections would
be delayed by two months. He however pointed out
that Comelec´s planning and preparation should not
have been delayed because there was no need for a
second bidding considering that one of the two bids should have been declared as responsive.
He then requested that his speech be immediately
referred to the Committee on Suffrage and Electoral Reforms so it may conduct an investigation in aid of legislation. He also said that per prior arrangement with the Committee on Rules, he will not answer interpellations related to his speech. 
(SOURCE: Journal No.56,p.5)

rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H081;
rows.abstract:
On the occasion of the 20 years of the Philippine
Mining Act of 1995 or Republic Act (RA) No. 7942,
Rep. Zarate reiterated the need to address the adverse consequences brought about by large-scale mining to the environment through the enactment of a new mining law to replace RA No. 7942. He argued that the mining law had failed its intended mandate to develop and conserve natural resources for national economic progress and protection of the affected people and indigenous communities. This, as he enumerated several grave environmental hazards that resulted from large-scale mining operations, including those caused by mining companies Marcopper, Lafayette, and Philex and others, that could be gleaned from the ongoing photo-exhibit in the North Lobby sponsored
jointly by the Committee on Indigenous Cultural
Communities and Indigenous Peoples and the
Committee on Natural Resources. Thereupon, Rep. Zarate explained that however substantial the contribution of the mining industry to the country´s economic progress, important consideration must be given to its social costs
particularly on the promotion of public health and the conservation of the natural resources. He proposed a complete restructuring of the Philippine Mining Act of 1995 and urged his peers to deliberate on House Bill No. 171 which seeks to promote scientific, propeople and proenvironment methods of mining. He recommended the repeal of RA No. 7942 for its failure to achieve its mandate. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.56,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-03-03
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H025;
rows.abstract:
In his speech, Rep. Erice said that to honor the 44 fallen members of the Philippine National Police Special Action Force (PNP-SAF), there is a need to pursue peace through the enactment of the
Bangsamoro Basic Law (BBL) as requested by the
President himself, but not after a thorough deliberation thereof without compromising the time element for its implementation before the 2016 elections. He noted that emotions over the incident are still high but suggested that the Ad Hoc Committee on the BBL should come up with a committee report on the matter before Congress takes a break on March 19 so the Members will have enough time to study it. Finally, Rep. Erice took exception on the recent statements of some leaders of the United Nationalist Alliance (UNA) and several party-list groups regarding their accusation that Malacañang was pressuring the House of Representatives to stop the investigation of the Mamasapano incident to cover up the blunder of President Benigno S. Aquino III on the
implementation of Oplan Exodus and to protect the
real culprit behind the death of the SAF 44. He
explained that the investigation was postponed to give way to several investigations conducted by separate bodies like the Senate and the PNP Board of Inquiry with the cooperation of all concerned government officials. He condemned the allegations of whitewash and coverups being asserted by UNA considering that it is a coalition partner of the Liberal Party in the House. In light thereof, he requested the Liberal Party in the House to reconsider its terms of coalition with the UNA Party. 
MANIFESTATION OF REP. TINIO
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Tinio raised three
concerns relative to the speech of Rep. Erice: 1)
Makabayan Party-List is consistent in its criticism of the police with respect to violations of civil rights of Filipino citizens, such as brutality, suppression of human rights, torture of citizens under arrest or police detention, and corruption in the police force; 2) he is in favor of continuing the discussion on the BBL but
President Aquino must be accountable for the failed implementation of the police operation that resulted in the Mamasapano incident; and 3) he stands by his position that there is a whitewash in the investigation of the incident especially with regard to the accountability of Cabinet officials and officers involved therein.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. TAMBUNTING
On motion of Rep. Romualdo, the Chair
recognized Rep. Gus S. Tambunting who expressed
sadness over the dragging of the name of Vice
President Jejomar Binay and UNA Party as the enemy
of the House. He pointed out that the Members of the UNA Party in the House had shown its support to the House leadership and to the President by supporting priority measures of the Executive. He also stated that he had filed a resolution on postponing the BBL deliberations until after they finished the investigation on the death of the 44 SAF members. Rep. Tambunting explained that Rep. Erice should have allowed a clarification of the issues that had been raised in his speech pertaining to Vice President Binay and UNA. As a member of UNA, he is compelled to defend his party mates and Vice President Binay and make known their party stand in the Chamber regarding certain issues, particularly with regard to the BBL.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Jose L.
Atienza Jr. maintained that Rep. Erice´s speech
assailing Vice President Binay and his capacity and integrity as Vice President of the country is a purely political innuendo to destroy the image and achievements of the Vice President who, he opined, is touted to become the next President of the Philippines. He explained that the political party of President Aquino, the Liberal Party, that has now evolved allegedly into a political party of lies, underachievement, and gross insensitivity in governance, has not stopped denigrating Vice
President Binay in the Senate and in all forms of
broadcast and print media. He claimed that Rep.
Erice´s unfounded accusations against Vice President Binay should be answered in the Plenary Hall in view of the fact that the Vice President has not been convicted in court of the accusations charged against him. Moreover, in ascribing wrongdoings in the course of official duties and unfounded accusations against the Vice President, Rep. Erice is diverting the real issue of blatant failure and criminal neglect of the PNoy Administration to bring about economic progress and alleviate the conditions of poor Filipinos.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.57,pp.4-5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-03-03
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Reps. Tinio, Tambunting and Atienza. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: C072;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Lobregat emphasized the details of the
workings of the Ad Hoc Committee on the BBL, which
included the number of public hearings it had
conducted in the House and other places in the country, as well as what had transpired during its executive sessions following the Mamasapano incident last January 25, 2015. Among other things, he noted that the Ad Hoc Committee encountered an apparent attempt to railroad the approval of the draft BBL during its January 27 executive session when a motion was put forward for the members to simply submit their proposed amendments in writing to be taken up on a later date. He explained further that in view of the massacre of the members of the PNP-SAF in Mamasapano, the Ad Hoc Committee had decided to postpone further Committee hearings on the BBL pending the submission of a committee report from the Special Committee on Peace, Reconciliation, and Unity and the Committee on Public Order and Safety which had been conducting a joint investigation of the Mamasapano incident. Thereupon, Rep. Lobregat informed the Body of what had transpired during the February 11, 2015 Committee hearing of the two Committees. Rep. Lobregat continued to vent his frustrations
over the postponement of the House committee
hearings on the Mamasapano incident when the Senate has already conducted several hearings; and the PNPBOI, Department of Justice (DOJ), National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and Commission on Human Rights (CHR) are continuing their respective
investigations. The Moro Islamic Liberation Front
(MILF), he said, is also conducting its own
investigation but has indicated it will submit the results of its inquiry to the Malaysian facilitator and not to the Philippine government. 
Continuation:  Admitting that the first House hearing on the Mamasapano incident was disrupted, Rep. Lobregat said that there are ways and means that could be implemented to improve the handling of future hearings. While a large group of House Members had written a letter to the Speaker appealing for the resumption of the Mamasapano inquiry, Rep. Lobregat averred that a Deputy Speaker was quoted as saying in an Interaction.com article that the House leadership had decided to archive its own probe because an inquiry by the House would just be a surplusage. He then made an appeal to the House leadership to immediately resume the House hearings on the Mamasapano incident for the sake of the integrity of the House.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ACEDILLO
On the initial query of Rep. Acedillo as to why the Mamasapano hearings should not be archived, Rep. Lobregat replied that he really does not know the reason for such decision which was why he decided to take the floor and ask the House leadership to allow the Body to continue its own probe on the incident. At this point, Reps. Acedillo and Lobregat agreed that the hearings in the House should continue because the Members were representatives of the people; the Body had legislative and oversight functions to fulfill
as a separate chamber of Congress; the other inquiries were held behind closed doors; the public was clamoring for truth and information; and the BOI report was limited in coverage and delayed. 
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Upon Rep. Romualdo´s motion, the Chair next
recognized Rep. Atienza who concurred with Rep.
Lobregat that the hearings should resume and should have been collegially and not unilaterally suspended; and that Committee hearings are held in aid of legislation. Both Members also agreed that there are no political intentions in their desire for the House to continue its investigation on the Mamasapano incident as they only want to ferret out the truth on the matter and be guided accordingly in the deliberations on the proposed BBL. Thereupon, Rep. Atienza urged his colleagues and the leadership of the House to join and heed the call of Rep. Lobregat to resume the investigation on the Mamasapano incident for the Members to deliberate on the proposed BBL in a nonpolitical and nonpartisan manner.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. PAGDILAO
Reps. Lobregat and Pagdilao initially discussed
whether the House should proceed with its inquiry on the Mamasapano incident even before the PNP-BOI
has submitted its report on the incident; the protocol by which House Committees could suspend its proceedings or cancel its deliberation and
investigation on an issue; and the legislative purpose and the lessons that can be learned as a result of such investigation. On whether the investigation by the House would only be superfluous because the Senate had already
conducted one, Rep. Lobregat said that in the absence of a joint hearing, the House should also have its own. Rep. Pagdilao expressed support for the resumption of the House inquiry on the Mamasapano incident. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.57,pp.5-7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-03-04
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Acedillo, Atienza and Pagdilao. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.abstract:

and friends to senseless violence and killings, citing for instance the death of the 44 Special Action Force (SAF) members in the Mamasapano incident and the recent murder of a barangay chairperson from her district. She underscored that only evil, selfishness and arrogance characterize violence and killings.

rows.author: G099;
rows.abstract:
In celebration of Women´s Month, Rep. Villarica
spoke about the significance of the role of women in politics, leadership and governance in a truly democratic society. She then cited several bills that the Committee on Women and Gender Equality which she chairs, has deemed important and urgent in advancing women´s rights, including among others the bills that seek to: 1) create a crisis center in every province and city of the country; 2) amend the AVAWC Law to cover cases of electronic violence; 3) amend the AntiSexual
Harassment Act to include all forms of sexual
harassment, including peer-to-peer sexual harassment; and 4) punish discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity. More importantly, she pointed out that the Committee had thoroughly worked hard especially in the measures seeking to amend the Family Code of the Philippines, so that appropriate amendments may be introduced on the floor. She then appealed to the House leadership to give the Committee
the opportunity to defend them on the floor not
only for the benefit of the poor, those in difficult circumstances, or victims of abuse, but for all the women in their lives. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.58,p.5)

rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.abstract:

from the Third District of Pangasinan shared her sentiments and thoughts on the plight of women in armed conflict situations. rows.abstract:
Rep. Ermita-Buhain focused on empowering women in the countryside through entrepreneurship. She talked about the Kilusang Kababaihan sa Unang
Distrito in her province where women were taught to unite, learn skills and embark on small businesses; linked to private aid groups; and tied in with the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA). Teaching entrepreneurship, she therefore stressed, was like planting trees that will bear much fruit.

rows.author: H037;
rows.abstract:
Next recognized by the Chair upon Rep. Antonino´s
motion, Rep. Elisa “Olga” T. Kho from the Second
District of Masbate paid tribute to women pioneers
in the medical profession. She first relayed the
academic and professional history of Dr. Honoria
Acosta-Sison, who pursued medicine when all doctors in the country were males and women were ashamed to consult them about gynecological ailments. Next relaying the academic and medical careers of Drs. Olivia Salamanca, Maria Paz Mendoza-Guazon, and Fe Del Mundo, Rep. Kho stated that the difficulties and challenging events in the lives of these women physicians have brought hope in the hearts and minds of women medical practitioners as they overcame obstacles in order to provide the best medical service to their countrymen. She said that honoring these pioneering female physicians compels future generations to become more involved and meaningful in their own service and that the legacies of these female doctors are a source of pride as well as a challenge to all women. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.58,p.7)

rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G105;
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. De Jesus echoed the
voices of the widows of the SAF Fallen 44 and the
women and children caught in the crossfire in the
Mamasapano tragedy in seeking for truth, justice and accountability. In order to achieve the same, she requested the House leadership to resume the joint inquiry of the Committee on Public Order and Safety and the Special Committee on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity on the Mamasapano incident considering that the government is calling for an all-out war as an answer to the worsening peace and order situation in Mindanao.
In celebration of Women´s Month, Rep. De Jesus
enjoined her colleagues to fight for truth, justice and accountability for women and other victims of violations in the peace process in Mindanao. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.58,pp.7&8)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-03-09
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F036;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Hofer underscored feminine power, this as
she pointed to the speeches earlier delivered by her
female colleagues alluding to the women sector as a
force to contend with. As she emphasized how world
leaders have recognized the rights and power of
women, she stressed the need to rediscover the
feminine power to love and nurture, and create
harmony and peace. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.58,p.8)

rows.author: H081;
rows.abstract:
Initially, Rep. Zarate called for the immediate
resumption of the investigation on the Mamasapano
incident which, he opined, was very imperative.
At this juncture, Deputy Speaker Balindong
relinquished the Chair to Rep. Banal. With the House leadership suspending the Body´s own hearing of the incident, Rep. Zarate spoke about his concerns on critical issues, such as the credibility of the Philippine National Police-Board of Inquiry´s (PNP-BOI) investigation; the importance of the House continuing its own hearing in the greater interest of justice and transparency; and the responsibility of the
President as the Commander-in-Chief especially in an operation as big and vital as Oplan Exodus.
Rep. Zarate then shared the following to his
colleagues: 1) the highlights of the Fact Finding
Mission which he joined in Tukanalipao,
Mamasapano, Maguindanao on February 9-11, 2015;
2) the accounts of the residents in the said area; and 3) the deep involvement of the United States in the incident. He enjoined his colleagues to fulfill their mandate as legislators and resume the hearings on the Mamasapano incident, in order to attain truth and justice. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.59,p.8)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2015-03-10)
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F059;
rows.abstract:
In view of the upcoming 73rd anniversary of the
Araw ng Kagitingan on April 9, Rep. Roman spoke on 
the plight of the World War II veterans in the country. She stated that the historic events during the Bataan Death March embodied the valor of the veterans that made them the beacon of liberty. She lamented however that the government has not been performing its constitutional mandate of providing immediate and adequate care for the veterans as their pensions and benefits remained unchanged for the last 20 years. As the Representative of the First District of Bataan and Chairperson of the Committee on Veterans Affairs, Rep. Roman underscored the sad plight of the
living veterans, and referred to the law as well as the constitutional mandate of providing them and their families with adequate assistance and care. She thereafter enjoined her colleagues to support the bill seeking to increase their pensions, which have remained unchanged for the past 20 years, and provide funds for the immediate payment of benefits due them.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.61,pp.29-30)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-03-16
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: F102;
rows.abstract:
VALEDICTORY SPEECH OF REP. BELLO (W.)
Stating at the outset that he will not entertain any question relative to his speech, Rep. Bello then explained his reasons for resigning as a Representative of Party-List Akbayan in the House of Representatives. He stressed in particular that he can no longer support his party´s stand of supporting Pres. Benigno S. Aquino III so he decided to resign out of respect for his party´s leadership and in conformity with Akbayan´s Code of Conduct. Rep. Bello pointed out that he did his best to remain an ally of the PNoy Administration by supporting its vital measures such as the Reproductive Health (RH) Law, the Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) Program, and the draft Bangsamoro Basic Law (BBL), as well as by emphasizing the unquestioned democratic legitimacy of the PNoy government. He however expressed his opposing stance on important issues such as the Disbursement Acceleration Program (DAP), retention of some inept and corrupt officials and the President´s behavior towards the Mamasapano
tragedy. He expressed appreciation for the courtesy and respect that was accorded to him by his House colleagues in the past six years but said that he will never forget the act that led to a charge against him of violating parliamentary courtesy in the Committee on Ethics during the 15th Congress. He then thanked and gave high regard for the opportunity of having worked with Speaker Belmonte and the entire House leadership; certain Members from the present and past
Congresses with whom he had worked closely; the
House Secretariat led by the Secretary General; the secretariat of the Committees on Overseas Workers Affair (which he chaired), Foreign Affairs, and Suffrage and Electoral Reforms; his congressional staff, and his friends from the House media. He then requested for the House to 1) extend hospitality and courtesy to his replacement, Ms. Angie Kato of Zamboanga; 2) pass the draft BBL which he deems a precondition for peace in Mindanao; 3)reopen the House investigation on the Mamasapano incident; 4) pass the amendment to the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program Extension with Reforms (CARPER) Law; and 5) enact the Freedom of Information Bill into law. He ended his valedictory speech by conveying to the President how he will not forget the times they fought on the side and appealing to the latter to accept responsibility for the Mamasapano incident. While he will leave the House on March 19 with a heavy heart, he emphasized that
he will treasure all the moments he spent there. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.61,pp.30-31)

rows.abstract:
Rep. Acedillo said that for the third time, he stands to warn Congress and the people of an impending danger to the Philippine national security right at its doorstep. He again talked about China´s activities in the South China Sea or West Philippine Sea which, he stressed, threatened Philippine sovereignty and economic well being. He initially described the geography, natural resources, oil potential, and environmental state of the area before subsequently discussing China´s dredging activities, building of harbor, airstrip, and commercial structures; and reclamation efforts therein as well as the presence of its navy forces. He pointed out how China had wantonly disregarded the Code of Conduct governing
the area, while troops and facilities in Philippine occupied islands remained inadequate for the last 20 years and the rehabilitation thereof continued to be resisted by the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) for fear of a backlash.
Rep. Acedillo thereafter asked President Aquino
and national leaders, the Filipino people, and the
National Security Council to act on and address
Chinese aggression in the West Philippine Sea as he warned that the discovery of gas and oil in the disputed area would spark another crisis. He opined that nobody will defend the Philippines but the Filipinos; and the tripartite strategy of arbitration, diplomatic protest, and ASEAN cooperation was useless and will bind the
initiatives of the departments and agencies concerned. He called for Philippine gallantry and heroism as was shown in the last stand in Bataan during the Second World War.

Rep. Ilagan took the floor to 1) thank the nation
for standing behind Filipino migrant worker Mary
Jane Veloso who was sentenced to death by execution in Indonesia on April 29, 2015, but was given a reprieve on the same day by the Indonesian

rows.author: H069;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Hicap first adverted to the recent celebration of Labor Day where different sectors led by the All Workers Unity, Kilusang Mayo Uno and Confederation for Unity, Recognition and
Advancement of Government Employees, clamored
for a national minimum wage of P16,000 a month.
Subsequently, he stressed that the current minimum
wage was not enough to provide for the basic needs of a family of six.  Citing statistics and survey results showing the disparity in the income generated by businesses and foreign investors compared to the meager salaries given to workers, Rep. Hicap emphasized that the primary call of the workers, both private and public, is to have a P16,000 national minimum wage considering that their meager salaries could not provide better lives for their families. To address the sufferings of the workers, Rep. Hicap enjoined his colleagues to legislate a national wage increase, repeal contractualization and the twotiered

rows.author: F100;
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino to celebrate International
Nurses´ Day the following day, Rep. Colmenares´
speech centered on the unfair treatment of the
country´s nurses who labor for many hours and yet are not given just compensation. He said that while the Philippines is the number one exporter of nurses around the world, there are still
200,000 unemployed nurses and 300,000 misemployed nurses in the country. Citing the International Council of Nurses, he said that the deteriorating health services and provision of nursing human resources are caused by a health reform process
implemented through the structural adjustment
program of the World Bank and the International
Monetary Fund. In closing, Rep. Colmenares sought the help of his colleagues to give their full support to the country´s nurses and the nursing profession by upgrading their basic monthly pay to P25,000 and ensuring the adequate funding of public health services, among others.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. PAQUIZ
Initially, Rep. Paquiz thanked Rep. Colmenares
for his concern on the plight of the nurses in the
country and voiced her concern regarding the
inequities in the country´s health care delivery system. She then asked about the status of the upgrading to Salary Grade 15 of government nurses´ monthly pay and urged her colleagues to support all health workers in the country. Rep. Colmenares stressed that they should assert not only the rights of health workers and patients but also their right as Members of Congress as he pointed
out that the Executive did not prioritize nor allocate funds for a bill that the House had already passed on the issue at hand. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.67,p.1)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-05-11
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Paquiz. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F103;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Guanlao asserted that the Philippines must
change its rice policies and reexamine its agricultural development paradigm based on the pressures facing the agricultural industry. He enumerated the following recommendations that he had repeatedly made throughout his tenure: keep production costs low; protect agricultural resources from illegal activities; minimize wasteful production and consumption of rice
and other staples; strengthen the National Food
Authority (NFA); pass laws for stronger rice research and development; extend the effectivity of the Agricultural Competitiveness Enhancement Fund (ACEF); and develop uplands and urban spaces for food production. He also mentioned the measures he and his colleagues had already filed in this regard. In closing, he enjoined his colleagues to support House Bill No. 4378, declaring May 15 of every year as the national day for small farmers and fishermen, and House Resolution No. 1838, calling for food waste
minimization. 
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BRAVO
After first discussing with Rep. Bravo why, unlike
its neighbors, the country´s agriculture sector is not yet prepared for ASEAN integration, Rep. Guanlao underscored the need to subsidize irrigation fees; increase the subsidized price of rice from the NFA; and provide a free farm modernization program and credit access to Land Bank of the Philippines. The Members also agreed that since President Benigno S. Aquino III began his term, the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) has yet to release funds from the ACEF to finance its avowed purposes. They cited the urgent need for Congress to extend the lifespan of ACEF, and then discussed the government´s policy on
the importation of basic commodities like rice and
sugar.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BATOCABE
Speaking in Filipino, Reps. Guanlao and Batocabe
discussed the illegal conversion of prime agricultural lands into residential, commercial and industrial establishments. Rep. Guanlao also delved into the failure of the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) to implement the law governing land conversions, to determine the number of illegal conversion cases, and to identify those who are criminally liable. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.67,p.2)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-05-11
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Bravo and Batocabe. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: C403;
rows.abstract:
After initially giving a backgrounder on the creation, membership composition, powers and mandate of the National Security Council (NSC), Rep. Biazon cited the need to convene the NSC because of the following issues confronting the national security of the country: 1) the aggressive stance of China in the Spratly Islands; and 2) the statements made by the officials of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) and the possible scenarios that might happen regarding
the passage or nonpassage of the proposed Bangsamoro Basic Law (BBL). Rep. Biazon urged the government to develop a national position that will clearly state its policies and strategies in response to the developments in the Spratly Islands. He also suggested that the government
pursue its diplomatic campaign on the Spratlys issue through the United Nations, and focus its efforts on the crafting of an acceptable BBL.
He thereafter cited several opinions pointing to
possible violence in the event Congress fails to pass the proposed BBL, and reiterated the need for the immediate convening of the NSC and the reexamination of Republic Act No. 7077 or the “Citizen Armed Forces of the Philippines Reservist Act” to determine whether the nation is prepared to meet eventualities and mobilize its security forces. He added that Congress should come up with a BBL that would be acceptable to all sectors of society. INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA Rep. Atienza first sought clarification on the location
of Spratly Islands, this as he expressed apprehension over the government´s lack of interest to protect them. He then discussed with Rep. Biazon the possible options of the Philippine government so as to properly handle the issue, including among others, the latter´s suggestion that Filipino fishermen be allowed to fish in the Spratly waters but with the members of the Philippine Coast Guard as escorts and that the NSC
should reexamine the Mutual Defense  Treaty (MDT).INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA(Continuation)
Rep. Biazon gave a brief background on the
Senate ratification of the Visiting Forces Agreement (VFA) in the late 1990s and reiterated the necessity for the NSC to reexamine the MDT to determine whether or not the United States is still an ally of the Philippines. Rep. Atienza appealed to the Members to heed and support the call of Rep. Biazon for the NSC to convene so that a national consensus can be achieved on how to
deal with a problem that requires urgent action.
With regard to the concern of Rep. Biazon on the draft BBL, Rep . Atienza took exception to the
apparent intervention of Malaysia in the country´s internal affairs. He then promised to support any
measure that Congress will take to urge President
Aquino to act with utmost dispatch and concern on the Spratlys and BBL issues.  INTERPELLATION OF
DEPUTY SPEAKER PADILLA. Initially, Rep. Padilla expressed his support on the call of Reps. Biazon and Atienza for the NSC to convene as soon as possible to discuss the Spratlys issue; to explore and examine the diplomatic options recommended
by Rep. Biazon in handling the China dispute;
and to revisit the 1951 Mutual Defense Treaty (MDT) between the United States and the Philippines. Rep. Padilla further raised the significant effect to Philippine territorial boundaries and sovereignty of the touted “US government position” and the questionable
implementation of the provisions of the MDT on the
probable military and armed attacks on Philippine territories. He proposed that the Philippine government explore concrete alternatives rather than rely on the supposed provisions of the MDT on the defense of Philippine territories by the United States; more so, that the United States will only act on its own interests and upon consultation with the US Congress. He agreed with the proposed courses of action by Rep. Biazon particularly on convening the NSC to formulate
a definite policy on Philippine territories in the
Spratlys and review of the MDT, recourse to diplomatic solutions to territorial boundary problems, and joint exploration, development, and venture with other claimant countries. These alternatives and the encroachment and occupation of Philippine territories despite the MDT should compel the government to act on Philippine geopolitical interests in the West Philippine
Sea, he added. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.69,pp.5&6)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2015-05-13)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Atienza and Padilla.

rows.author: G105;
rows.title_short: Justice For The Kentex Fire Victims
rows.abstract:
In her speech delivered in Filipino, Rep. De Jesus
sought justice for the 72 workers, most of whom were women, who died in a fire that recently burned down the Kentex Manufacturing Corporation factory in Valenzuela City.  She thereafter referred to the Department of Labor and Employment´s (DOLE) efforts to clear the factory
owners from any responsibility over the said tragedy by declaring that it has complied with general labor standards and occupational safety measures. She however related the confirmed reports of the Institute for Occupational Health and Safety Development (IOHSD) about the poor and unsafe working conditions of Kentex employees, which she likened to death traps. She also took exception to DOLE Department Order No.131-13 or the Labor Laws Compliance System which in effect transfers the government´s responsibility to ensure the occupational health and safety of
the workers to firm owners and management by implementing a self-assessment system and a scheduled, rather than a surprise, inspection of a factory. She then called on her colleagues to support the call of the victims´ families seeking justice; investigate the growing labor contractualization and noncompliance of firms with occupational safety measures nationwide; and pass a law that safeguards safety, just compensation and regularization of workers.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. GUNIGUNDO
As the Representative of the district covering
Kentex factory, Rep. Gunigundo expressed interest in the proposed conduct of investigation concerning the negligence of DOLE and its issuance to Kentex of a certificate of compliance to general labor standards; as well as the proliferation of labor contractualization
and payment of salaries below the mandated minimum
wage. Rep. De Jesus confirmed that the Committee on Labor and Employment headed by chairperson Rep.
Karlo Alexei B. Nograles will conduct a meeting on
Wednesday, May 20, 2015 regarding the issue at hand. They next discussed Rep. Gunigundo´s following concerns: what encompasses the terms “occupational safety” and “fire safety”; the job of the labor law compliance officers (LLCO); the basis of the regional director of the DOLE-National Capital Region in granting a certificate of compliance to the company in 2014 and whether there was an anomaly when the LLCO and the Bureau of Fire Protection office concerned granted the pertinent permits to Kentex; and the provisions
of Republic Act (RA) No. 9514 or the “Fire Code of the Philippines” concerning the requirement of a fire safety inspection certification prior to the issuance of a mayor´s permit to a prospective business establishment. Rep. Gunigundo disagreed with the process being implemented by the City of Valenzuela on adopting its Citizen´s Charter in the grant or renewal of mayor´s permits to factories or establishments. Meanwhile, Rep. De Jesus suggested that Valenzuela City officials
be invited to the Committee hearing to shed light on the violations being committed in its implementation of RA No. 9514 as well as to pinpoint the persons accountable for the Kentex tragedy. Also to address the Kentex issue, Rep. De Jesus cited the following courses of action to be undertaken by the Gabriela Party-List and its allied organizations and network: filing of a Resolution for a congressional investigation and comprehensive review and study of actual experiences and occurrences of death among
workers who suffered or have been suffering from
smoke fumes and fire in various manufacturing companies; call for an inquiry on the implementation of the Occupational Health and Safety Law, the Fire Code and existing labor laws; a concrete commitment of legal aid services; aid in the processing of death benefits and privileges and provision of psychological group counselling for the families of the dead laborers; and reiteration of the rights and privileges of and social justice for all laborers and workers in the country.  (SOURCE: House Journal No. 70,pp.6-7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2015-05-19
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: H069;
rows.abstract:
On the occasion of the forthcoming 7th death anniversary of Rep. Crispin “Ka Bel” Beltran on May 20, 2015, Rep. Hicap reiterated to the Body Ka Bel´s selfless life as a labor leader and street parliamentarian and one of the pioneers of the militant labor movement in the country; a foremost proponent of labor unionism and labor rights; a strong oppositor to martial law, dictatorship and authoritarian rule; and who died a plain laborer,
unenriched by anomalies and graft and corruption.
He then underscored that if Ka Bel were only alive
today, he would be at the forefront of the militant labor movement and would be very vocal about the senseless deaths of numerous laborers from the fire that gutted the Kentex factory in Valenzuela City. He maintained that social justice for the Filipino worker remains a distant objective in these unfortunate incidents, particularly in the repeated occurrences of patent
abuse by the State and capitalists of workers´
rights and their violation of the occupational health and safety of laborers in the workplace. Voicing out the Kentex workers´ complaints including, among others, getting paid below the minimum wage rate, nonremittance by their recruitment agency of their Social Security System contributions, and the system of labor
contractualization, Rep. Hicap stated that his PartyList Anakpawis had earlier submitted a resolution calling for an investigation on the circumstances surrounding the Kentex tragedy.
In closing, he maintained that there is nothing
more significant in paying tribute to the memory of Ka Bel and to the lives that were lost in the Kentex fire than to continue the fight for the rights of the working class which Ka Bel had started. He added that justice should be given especially to the Kentex workers and other victims of violations of the country´s occupational health and safety standards. (SOURCE: House Journal No.70, p.7)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2015-05-18)

rows.author: F122;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Dela Cruz aired his concern on the political,
socioeconomic, and cultural issues surrounding the approval of the proposed Bangsamoro Basic Law (BBL). He also underscored the ramifications of the draft BBL as well as the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro and Framework Agreement, all containing the demands of the Bangsamoro people to exercise their right to self-determination and political and territorial
autonomy. He however opined that these do not resolve the problem of political autonomy for Muslim Mindanao as they violate the provisions of the 1987 Constitution, deprive the Filipinos of a sovereign nation, and might trigger an endless ethnic strife between Christian Filipinos and Muslims similar to the political situation in the Baltic republics, particularly in the former
Yugoslavia. Rep. Dela Cruz added that more alarming and which should be exposed and opposed is that taken in their totality, the acts of the negotiating panels and the Bangsamoro Transition Commission may have already committed treason in proposing an unconstitutional and unrealistic Bangsamoro Law since this may have already sold the country down the drain. In closing, and in commemoration of the tragic Mamasapano massacre, Rep. Dela Cruz urged everyone to stand fast and do the right thing and by the grace of the Almighty, overcome the sins and prejudices, animosities
and inequalities of the past and move on to glorious days as one, undivided country under the
grace of God. (SOURCE: House Jornal No.71,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2015-05-25
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: H063;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Acedillo said that China continues to maintain its aggressive posturing and effective control over the West Philippine Sea and the entire South China Sea in order to strengthen her territorial claim and safeguard her interest in the area. He described the expanded reclamation and construction activities in the seven Chinese-occupied reefs, three of which were within the Philippine exclusive economic zone (EEZ).
He cited the increasing deployment of Chinese cargo vessels, ships, and Coast Guard forces to patrol the vicinity of Scarborough and Ayungin Shoals and to harass Philippine vessels therein.
He also cited to the Body the actions taken by both the House and the Senate on the issue of the West Philippine Sea and the Spratly Islands, the economic and military implications, the threat to the energy security of the country on the continuing operation, reclamation and construction activities in the Chinese-occupied reefs which are within the Philippine EEZ, and the medium to long-term geopolitical implications of such occupation in the West Philippine Sea. Thereupon, Rep. Acedillo expressed belief that China, in disrupting the seaborne trade routes of goods
and oil by enforcing maritime and fishing regulations in the West Philippine Sea, seeks to fundamentally alter the balance of power in Asia, which has diminished the vitality of United States-Asian alliances that would ultimately displace the US as the preeminent power in
the Asia-Pacific region. He noted that despite the country´s efforts of pursuing an independent foreign policy, it cannot escape the realities of great power politics involving China and the US, this as he stressed that in the last 70 years,
only the latter has guaranteed continued security in the Asia-Pacific region. Finally, he asked whether China is trying to avoid a major confrontation with the US, as it has done before, or has now taken an action that will lead to war. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.71, p.7)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2015-05-25)
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: H081;
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Zarate adverted to the
P123 billion Laguna Lakeshore Expressway Dike, a
public-private partnership (PPP) project creating an offshore megadike in Laguna Lake and enumerated the numerous critical environmental and public infrastructure concerns that will affect the towns and communities of Biñan, Santa Rosa, San Pedro and Taguig located along Laguna Lake. He explained that the megadike project will not address the causes of the perennial flooding from Laguna Lake if the government were not to address first the problems of comprehensive dredging, reforestation and rehabilitation of watersheds, re-opening of the Napindan Hydraulic Control System, wastewater treatment and prevention of dumping of garbage in rivers and waterways, which he claimed were the primary causes of the flooding. He argued that the government´s approval of the megadike project will only allow private corporations and real estate developers to gain substantial profit through
a reclamation project and a six-lane expressway, endanger public safety during flooding and occurrences of earthquake as it is near the Marikina West Valley Fault System, and cause the eviction of coastal communities residing along Laguna Lake. He then sought the help of his colleagues representing Taguig, Muntinlupa, and Laguna to oppose the project. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 71,p.17)
